definition_zh: 陡峭的；险峻的；骤然的；轻率的
definition_en: very steep and high, or happening suddenly and without careful thought
core_image: 一步踏空就会滚落的峭壁，下方山谷深不见底
scene: 山道上没有护栏，脚下就是深谷。The path to the summit is extremely precipitous, so every step needs extra care.
sceneCN: 这里 precipitous 是「陡峭的、险峻的」（第 1 个义项：山坡陡得几乎站不住脚）；句意：通往山顶的小路极其陡峭，每一步都要格外小心。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 praecipitium 构成，义为「悬崖；绝壁」
由同源名词构成，义为「险境；边缘」
由 -ous 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「陡峭地；急剧地」
与 precipitous 同出 praecipitare，义为「促使（事件）仓促发生」
由 precipitate 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「降水；沉淀」

senses.title: So steep that it is nearly impossible to climb
senses.definition: describing a slope, cliff, or path so steep that walking up or down is dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 形容斜坡、悬崖或小路陡峭到上下行走都很危险的
senses.example: Climbers paused before the precipitous north face.
senses.exampleCN: 登山者在陡峭的北壁前停了下来。
senses.why: Latin praeceps means a place where one falls headlong, so the adjective first pictures a drop.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praeceps 指人一头栽下去的地方，所以这个形容词首先画出「向下坠落」的画面。

senses.title: Happening suddenly and very fast
senses.definition: describing a fall, rise, or change that is sudden and very large
senses.definitionCN: 形容下滑、上升或变化来得突然且幅度很大
senses.example: The company saw a precipitous fall in sales.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司经历了销售额的急剧下滑。
senses.why: A headlong plunge down a cliff becomes a number or price plunging just as fast.
senses.whyCN: 从峭壁上「一头栽下」的动作，被用来形容数字或价格以同样快的速度直线下跌。

senses.title: Acting too quickly without thinking
senses.definition: describing a choice, move, or action made in haste, without weighing the risks
senses.definitionCN: 形容选择、举动或行动匆忙作出，没有权衡风险
senses.example: Leaving school was a precipitous choice for such a young student.
senses.exampleCN: 对这样年轻的学生来说，退学是一个草率的决定。
senses.why: Someone who rushes headlong over an edge acts without looking, so the headlong image also paints rash conduct.
senses.whyCN: 一头冲向悬崖边的人根本没有看清脚下，所以「头朝前栽下」的画面也用来表现鲁莽的举动。

intro.en: Precipitous comes from Latin praeceps, meaning headlong, from prae and caput, and its strengthened form praecipitiosus, meaning full of steep drops.
intro.cn: precipitous 来自拉丁语 praeceps（头朝前的、倒栽的），由 prae（向前）与 caput（头）构成；其加强形式 praecipitiosus 意为「满是陡崖的」。

items.en: Praeceps joins prae, in front, with caput, head, and means head first.
items.cn: praeceps 把 prae（向前）与 caput（头）合在一起，意为「头朝前」。

items.en: The derived adjective praecipitiosus describes places full of steep falls.
items.cn: 由此派生的形容词 praecipitiosus 用来形容满是陡崖的地方。

items.en: French precipiteux carries the steep sense of the adjective toward English.
items.cn: 法语 precipiteux 把该形容词的「陡峭」义带向英语。

items.en: Precipitous is used in English for sheer cliffs and slopes.
items.cn: precipitous 在英语中用来形容陡直的悬崖与坡道。

items.en: The headlong image extends to sudden falls and rash actions.
items.cn: 「头朝前栽下」的画面又延伸到突然的下跌与鲁莽的举动。

note.en: Precipitous belongs to the cliff family, with precipice, precipitation, and abrupt, and it is close to other steep words such as steep and sheer.
note.cn: precipitous 属于「悬崖」一族，与 precipice、precipitation、abrupt 同源或同形，并与 steep、sheer 等表「陡」的词义域相邻。

entries.definition: a very steep rock face or cliff
rain, snow, or the chemical process of settling
in a hasty way
rising or falling sharply at a large angle
almost vertical
happening quickly and without warning

normalIntro.en: Precipitous keeps the picture of a head-first plunge over a cliff edge.
normalIntro.cn: precipitous 保留着「头朝前栽下悬崖」的画面。

normal.en: The root caput means head, and prae means in front.
normal.cn: 词根 caput 意为头，prae 意为向前。

normal.en: A cliff is precipitous when it drops almost vertically.
normal.cn: 悬崖近乎垂直地落下时就是 precipitous。

normal.en: A precipitous decline is a sharp fall in prices or health.
normal.cn: precipitous decline 指价格或健康状况的急剧下跌。

normal.en: A precipitous decision is a hasty one.
normal.cn: precipitous decision 指草率匆忙的决定。

normal.en: Compare steep: steep is neutral, precipitous adds danger and drama.
normal.cn: 对比 steep：steep 中性，precipitous 多了危险与紧张的色彩。

abstract.en: Picture a climber slipping right at the cliff edge.
abstract.cn: 想象登山者在悬崖边缘打了个趔趄。

abstract.en: Imagine a share price falling like water over a waterfall.
abstract.cn: 想象股价像瀑布的水一样直落而下。

abstract.en: Think of a man running into action without looking at the edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人根本不看脚下就冲向前去。

examples.en: The old road runs along a precipitous ridge for almost a mile.
examples.cn: 这条老路沿着险峻的山脊延伸了将近一英里。

examples.en: A precipitous rise in rents pushed many small shops out of town.
examples.cn: 租金的急剧上涨把许多小店挤出了城区。

examples.en: Investors saw the stock as a precipitous bet after the scandal.
examples.cn: 丑闻之后，投资者认为买这只股票是一次冒失的赌博。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕谁扑得死」——站在峭壁边上，怕谁一脚扑下去就没命；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 prae（向前）+ caput（头）→ praeceps（头朝前、倒栽）→ praecipitiosus（多陡崖的）→ 法语 → 英语 precipitous，核心义「一头栽下」。

sensesIntro.en: Precipitous starts with the physical cliff, extends to numbers that fall as fast as a plunge, and ends with rash action.
sensesIntro.cn: precipitous 从实体的悬崖出发，延伸到像坠落一样快速下行的数字，最后落在鲁莽轻率的行动上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slope so steep that a step would become a fall.
core.cn: 核心意象：陡得一步踩空就会坠落的山坡。

branches.en: The physical slope is the first and most concrete sense.
branches.cn: 实体的陡坡是最先出现的具体义项。

branches.en: A figure that plunges like a body over the edge is the sudden sense.
branches.cn: 像身体从边缘坠下般骤降的数字，是「急剧」义项。

branches.en: Acting without looking at the drop is the rash sense.
branches.cn: 不看脚下就行动，是「轻率」义项。

branches.en: A cliff and a rash act both demand caution before the first step.
branches.cn: 悬崖和草率行为都要求迈出第一步之前先谨慎。

branches.en: Traders who dump shares in haste often create a sudden fall.
branches.cn: 急于抛售股票的交易者常常造成骤然的下跌。

intro.en: Precipitous is a Latin compound of prae and caput, with English relatives such as precipice and precipitate.
intro.cn: precipitous 是 prae 与 caput 构成的拉丁复合词，英语中与 precipice、precipitate 同族。

latinIntro.en: Latin prae means before or in front, and caput means head.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prae 意为在前面，caput 意为头。

items.example: Prae- opens the compound praeceps.
items.exampleCN: prae- 开启复合词 praeceps。

items.example: Caput gives the head in praeceps.
items.exampleCN: caput 提供 praeceps 中「头」的部分。

items.example: Praeceps describes a headlong fall.
items.exampleCN: praeceps 描述头朝前栽下。

items.example: Praecipitium is the steep place itself.
items.exampleCN: praecipitium 就是陡崖本身。

items.example: Praecipitiosus is the direct Latin ancestor.
items.exampleCN: praecipitiosus 是直接的拉丁祖先。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ous turns a noun into precipitous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 把名词变成 precipitous。

items.example: Precipice keeps the cliff meaning.
items.exampleCN: precipice 保留「悬崖」义。

items.meaning: to cause to happen too soon
items.example: Precipitate keeps the hasty sense.
items.exampleCN: precipitate 保留「仓促」义。

items.meaning: in a steep or hasty way
items.example: The adverb takes the suffix -ly.
items.exampleCN: 副词形式加上后缀 -ly。

definition_zh: 前兆；先兆；先驱；（物质的）前体
definition_en: a person or thing that comes before and signals something that will follow
core_image: 跑在前面的报信人在队伍到来之前先赶到村口
scene: 暴风雨来临之前，气压计先悄悄下降。A sharp drop in air pressure is often a precursor of a violent storm.
sceneCN: 这里 precursor 是「前兆、先兆」（第 1 个义项：预示某事将要发生的迹象）；句意：气压急剧下降往往是暴风雨的前兆。

derivatives.zh: 由 -or 换成 -ory 构成，义为「先兆的；前期的」
较罕见的名词，由同一词干构成，义为「预兆；预示」

senses.title: An early sign of something coming
senses.definition: a sign or event that shows something more important is about to happen
senses.definitionCN: 预示更重要的事情即将发生的迹象或事件
senses.example: Headaches can be a precursor of a migraine.
senses.exampleCN: 头痛可能是偏头痛的前兆。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to run before, so a precursor is a runner that arrives ahead of the main event.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「跑在前面」，所以前兆就是先于主事件跑到现场的报信者。

senses.title: A person or work that prepares the way
senses.definition: a person, idea, or earlier version of something that leads the way for later ones
senses.definitionCN: 为后来者开辟道路的人物、思想或更早的版本
senses.example: The small workshop was a precursor of the modern factory.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小作坊是现代工厂的先驱。
senses.why: An earlier version of a thing runs the same road first, so it is called the forerunner of what follows.
senses.whyCN: 某个东西的更早版本先跑过同一条路，所以被称为后来者的先驱。

senses.title: A substance used to make another
senses.definition: a chemical substance from which another substance is produced in a reaction
senses.definitionCN: 在反应中用来生成另一种物质的化学物质
senses.example: The body turns the amino acid into a precursor of serotonin.
senses.exampleCN: 人体把这种氨基酸转变成血清素的前体。
senses.why: The chemical sense keeps the order: the precursor comes first in the process and the product runs after it.
senses.whyCN: 化学义保留了先后顺序：前体在过程中先出现，产物随后而来。

intro.en: Precursor comes from Latin praecursor, a forerunner, from praecurrere, to run before, built from prae and currere.
intro.cn: precursor 来自拉丁语 praecursor（先行者、报信人），源于 praecurrere（跑在前面），由 prae（在前）与 currere（跑）构成。

items.en: Currere means to run, and prae- means before, so praecurrere means to run ahead.
items.cn: currere 意为跑，prae- 意为在前，所以 praecurrere 意为跑在前面。

items.en: Praecursor names a forerunner, a scout, or a herald.
items.cn: praecursor 指先行者、侦察兵或报信人。

items.en: The word enters English first through religious and literary language, naming someone who announces a coming figure.
items.cn: 十六世纪的英语先从宗教与文学语言中借用该词，指预告重要人物到来的人。

items.en: The meaning widens to any sign, event, or earlier form that comes before another.
items.cn: 含义扩大到任何先于另一事物出现的迹象、事件或早期形态。

items.en: Chemistry adds a technical sense for a substance that leads to a product.
items.cn: 化学又增添了专业义：导向产物的前体物质。

note.en: Precursor belongs to the running family with cursory, incursion, and concurrent, and it sits close to forerunner and precursor-like words such as omen and antecedent.
note.cn: precursor 属于「跑」词族，与 cursory、incursion、concurrent 同源，义域上靠近 forerunner，以及 omen、antecedent 一类词。

entries.definition: done quickly without attention to detail
a sudden brief invasion
serving as a sign of something to come
a person or thing that came before another
a sign of what will happen
something that came before in time

normalIntro.en: Precursor keeps the picture of someone running ahead to announce what is coming.
normalIntro.cn: precursor 保留着「有人先跑一步去报信」的画面。

normal.en: The Latin currere means to run, as in current and course.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 currere 意为跑，与 current、course 同源。

normal.en: A precursor comes before, so it is the first runner in the race.
normal.cn: precursor 先于其他事物，是赛跑中跑在最前面的那个人。

normal.en: A precursor to war means an early sign of war.
normal.cn: a precursor to war 指战争的早期迹象。

normal.en: In chemistry a precursor is a starter substance.
normal.cn: 在化学中 precursor 是起始物质。

normal.en: Compare forerunner: it is plainer and more physical, precursor is more formal.
normal.cn: 对比 forerunner：它更朴素、更实体，precursor 更正式。

abstract.en: Picture a scout on the mountain path long before the army.
abstract.cn: 想象大部队还很远时，侦察兵已站在山路上。

abstract.en: Imagine a small craft shop that slowly grows into a huge factory.
abstract.cn: 想象一间小手工坊慢慢长成了巨大的工厂。

abstract.en: Think of two dominoes, the first one leaning onto the second.
abstract.cn: 想象两块多米诺骨牌，第一块斜靠在第二块上。

examples.en: The early flood may have been a precursor to the great famine.
examples.cn: 早年的那场洪水也许是大饥荒的前兆。

examples.en: Radio was a precursor of television as mass entertainment.
examples.cn: 作为大众娱乐，广播是电视的先驱。

examples.en: Chemists heated the precursor until the crystals formed.
examples.cn: 化学家加热前体，直到晶体生成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑去可死」——报信的人抢在前面扑出去，命都不要；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 prae（在前）+ currere（跑）→ praecurrere（跑在前面）→ praecursor（先行者；报信人）→ 英语 precursor，核心义「跑在前面的人或物」。

sensesIntro.en: Precursor starts with a sign that runs ahead of an event, widens to an earlier person or version, and ends with a starting substance in chemistry.
sensesIntro.cn: precursor 先是先于事件出现的迹象，再扩展到更早出现的人或版本，最后落在化学中的起始物质上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a herald running ahead of the main body.
core.cn: 核心意象：报信人跑在大队人马前面先到。

branches.en: The early sign is the most common everyday sense.
branches.cn: 早期迹象是最常见的日常义项。

branches.en: An earlier person or version is the forerunner sense.
branches.cn: 更早出现的人或版本是「先驱」义项。

branches.en: A starting substance in a reaction is the technical sense.
branches.cn: 反应中的起始物质是专业义项。

branches.en: Both a sign and an earlier version arrive before the main event.
branches.cn: 先兆与早期版本都在主事件之前到达。

branches.en: A forerunner and a chemical precursor both come first in the chain.
branches.cn: 先驱与化学前体都处在链条的最前端。

intro.en: Precursor pairs the Latin prefix prae- with currere, to run, and the English running family around it is large.
intro.cn: precursor 把拉丁前缀 prae- 与 currere（跑）搭配起来，围绕它的英语「跑」词族十分庞大。

latinIntro.en: Latin prae- means before, and currere means to run.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语前缀 prae- 意为在前，currere 意为跑。

items.example: Pre- marks something that comes earlier.
items.exampleCN: pre- 标记更早出现的事物。

items.example: Currere supplies the running image.
items.exampleCN: currere 提供「跑」的意象。

items.example: Praecurrere joins prefix and verb.
items.exampleCN: praecurrere 把前缀与动词合在一起。

items.example: Praecursor is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: praecursor 是直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -or marks the doer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 标记动作的执行者。

items.example: Precursory keeps the early-sign sense.
items.exampleCN: precursory 保留「早期迹象」义。

items.example: Cursory shares the running root.
items.exampleCN: cursory 与它共享「跑」词根。

items.meaning: running together at the same time
items.example: Concurrent adds the prefix con-.
items.exampleCN: concurrent 由前缀 con- 构成。

items.example: Incursion runs into a place.
items.exampleCN: incursion 是跑进某个地方。

definition_zh: 前任；前身；（被取代的）旧型号
definition_en: the person who had a job, position, or thing before someone else
core_image: 办公室门上刚换下的名牌，照片换成了一张新面孔
scene: 新校长走进办公室，桌上还放着前一任校长留下的文件。The new head teacher quickly changed the policies of her predecessor.
sceneCN: 这里 predecessor 是「前任」（第 1 个义项：在同一职位上前于某人的人）；句意：新校长很快改变了前任的政策。

derivatives.zh: 由 prae- 与 cedere 同源的 -cess 加 -ion 构成，义为「先行；岁差」
较罕见的同根名词，义为「前任；先行者」
由前缀 sub-（代替）加同根 -cessor 构成，义为「继任者」
由 succedere 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「继承；连续」
玩笑式生造词，由 predecessor 加 -ness 构成，义为「没有前任的状态」

senses.title: The person who held a job before you
senses.definition: a person who had a particular job or position before the present holder
senses.definitionCN: 在现任者之前担任某个职务或职位的人
senses.example: My predecessor left a detailed list of notes for me.
senses.exampleCN: 我的前任给我留下了一份详细的笔记清单。
senses.why: Latin decedere means to go away or depart, so a predecessor is the one who went before along the same path.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 decedere 意为离开、走开，所以前任是沿着同一条路先走一步的人。

senses.title: An earlier thing that the present one replaced
senses.definition: a machine, system, or product that came before the current version and was replaced by it
senses.definitionCN: 先于当前版本出现、后来被其取代的机器、系统或产品
senses.example: This phone is much lighter than its predecessor.
senses.exampleCN: 这款手机比它的上一代轻得多。
senses.why: Objects also follow one another along a path, so the older machine is the same kind of thing that came first.
senses.whyCN: 物品也会沿着一条路线更替，所以旧机器就是同类事物中先出现的那个。

senses.title: A thing that leads to a later stage
senses.definition: an early form or stage from which a later thing develops, especially in history or biology
senses.definitionCN: 后来的事物由其发展而来的早期形态或阶段，尤用于历史或生物学
senses.example: Ancient trade routes were the predecessors of modern highways.
senses.exampleCN: 古代商路是现代高速公路的前身。
senses.why: When a later form grows out of an earlier one, the earlier form is seen as having gone ahead first.
senses.whyCN: 当后来的形态从更早的形态长出来时，早先的那个就被看作先走一步的东西。

intro.en: Predecessor comes from Latin praedecessor, one who goes before, from prae and decedere, which means to depart.
intro.cn: predecessor 来自拉丁语 praedecessor（先行者、前辈），由 prae（在前）与 decedere（离开、走开）构成。

items.en: Decedere joins de-, away, with cedere, to go, and means to depart.
items.cn: decedere 把 de-（离开）与 cedere（走）合在一起，意为离开、走开。

items.en: Praedecessor names someone who went before, an elder or a forebear.
items.cn: praedecessor 指在先走过的人、长辈或先人。

items.en: The form passeur hands the word to medieval French usage.
items.cn: 中世纪法语借入该词并加以使用。

items.en: English borrows the word for an ancestor or an earlier holder of an office.
items.cn: 英语借入该词，用来指祖先或先前担任某职务的人。

items.en: The office sense becomes dominant, and the meaning widens to earlier models and systems.
items.cn: 职务义成为主流，含义又扩展到更早的型号与系统。

note.en: Predecessor shares the going root cedere with the cess and cede family, and it is close to forerunner and ancestor.
note.cn: predecessor 与 predecessor 系列词、以 cess 为干的形式共享「走」词根 cedere，义域上靠近 forerunner 与 ancestor。

entries.definition: a rare word for a predecessor
entries.definitionCN: 罕见词，与 predecessor 同根，义为「前任」

the act of giving up land or rights
an earlier person or thing that came before
a person from whom you are descended

normalIntro.en: Predecessor keeps the image of the person who walked down the corridor before you reached the office.
normalIntro.cn: predecessor 保留着「有人比你早一步走过同一条走廊」的画面。

normal.en: Pre- means before, and cedere means to go.
normal.cn: pre- 意为在前，cedere 意为走。

normal.en: Your predecessor is the person who had your job before you.
normal.cn: your predecessor 就是在你之前担任你这份工作的人。

normal.en: The predecessor model is the older version of a product.
normal.cn: the predecessor model 就是产品的上一代。

normal.en: Successor is the opposite partner of predecessor.
normal.cn: successor 是 predecessor 的反义搭档。

normal.en: Compare forerunner: forerunner is broader, predecessor is stronger for jobs and models.
normal.cn: 对比 forerunner：forerunner 更宽泛，predecessor 更强调职位与型号。

abstract.en: Picture a name plate just taken down from a door.
abstract.cn: 想象一块刚从门上取下的名牌。

abstract.en: Imagine a relay runner handing the baton over at the line.
abstract.cn: 想象接力赛跑者在终点线前交出接力棒。

abstract.en: Think of an old letter that a new letter continues.
abstract.cn: 想象一封新的信在接着一封旧信往下写。

examples.en: The new manager spent a week reviewing the files left by her predecessor.
examples.cn: 新经理花了一周时间查看前任留下的文件。

examples.en: The laptop is faster and slimmer than its predecessor.
examples.cn: 这款笔记本电脑比上一代更快、更薄。

examples.en: Horse carriages were the predecessors of early motor cars.
examples.cn: 马车是早期汽车的前身。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不如得瑟色」——前任爱得瑟，不如新任踏实；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 prae（在前）+ decedere（离开、走开）→ praedecessor（先去的人）→ 英语 predecessor，核心义「沿着同一条路先走的那一位」。

sensesIntro.en: Predecessor first means the person who went before you, then the earlier model that was replaced, and finally an early stage that led to a later form.
sensesIntro.cn: predecessor 先指早于你担任某职的人，再指被取代的更早型号，最后指导向后来形态的更早阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walker who took the same path one step earlier.
core.cn: 核心意象：早一步走过同一条路的先行者。

branches.en: The holder of the same office is the personal sense.
branches.cn: 同一职位的先前担任者是「人」的义项。

branches.en: An earlier replaced model is the product sense.
branches.cn: 被取代的更早型号是产品义项。

branches.en: An early stage leading to a later form is the historical sense.
branches.cn: 导向后来形态的早期阶段是历史义项。

branches.en: Both a colleague before you and an older model go before the current one.
branches.cn: 职位上的前任与旧型号都先于当前的那个出现。

branches.en: Every replaced product is also a stage that leads toward a later design.
branches.cn: 每个被取代的产品同时也是通往后续设计的阶段。

intro.en: Predecessor combines the Latin prefix prae- with decedere, to depart, and shares the going root with successor and cession.
intro.cn: predecessor 结合拉丁前缀 prae- 与 decedere（离开），与 successor、cession 共享「走」词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin prae- means before, and cedere means to go, to yield, or to withdraw.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语前缀 prae- 意为在前，cedere 意为走、让出或退开。

items.example: Prae- marks the one who goes first.
items.exampleCN: prae- 标记先走的那一位。

items.example: Cedere supplies the going image.
items.exampleCN: cedere 提供「走」的意象。

items.example: Decessus literally means a going away.
items.exampleCN: decessus 字面意为「走开」。

items.example: Praedecessor is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: praedecessor 是直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -or marks the person.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 标记「人」。

items.example: Decessor drops the prefix.
items.exampleCN: decessor 去掉了前缀。

items.example: Successor pairs with sub- and the same root.
items.exampleCN: successor 由 sub- 与同一词根构成。

items.example: Cessation keeps cedere in a stopping sense.
items.exampleCN: cessation 以「停下」义保留 cedere。

items.meaning: a going before, a slow rotation
items.example: Precession also builds on pre- and cedere.
items.exampleCN: precession 也由 pre- 与 cedere 构成。

definition_zh: 困境；窘境；尴尬的处境；难以摆脱的难题
definition_en: an unpleasant and difficult situation that is hard to escape or solve
core_image: 一个人被三面围墙困住，只剩一条窄路，却看不见出口
scene: 项目截止前一天，合作伙伴突然撤资，负责人面对空空的账户和满屋的同事。A day before the deadline the partner pulled out, leaving the manager in a predicament she had never planned for.
sceneCN: 这里 predicament 是「困境、窘境」（第 1 个义项：进退两难的糟糕处境）；句意：项目截止前一天，合作伙伴突然撤资，负责人陷入一个她从未预料到的困境。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -al 构成的形容词，义为「困境的；与窘境相关的」，属罕见书面用法
同一拉丁语词根 praedicare 的缩略同族词，义为「布道；说教」，与名词 predicament 拼写和意义都已相距很远
同源名词 predicare 的派生形容词，义为「表语的；断定性的」，主要用于语法与逻辑领域

senses.title: A difficult and unpleasant situation
senses.definition: an awkward and difficult situation that is hard to get out of
senses.definitionCN: 令人尴尬、难以摆脱的困难处境
senses.example: The company found itself in a serious predicament after the funding was cut.
senses.exampleCN: 资金被削减后，公司发现自己陷入了严重的困境。
senses.why: The Latin verb praedicare means to declare publicly, and from the idea of a state that has been declared came the sense of a fixed condition one is placed in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 praedicare 意为「公开宣告」，由「被宣告的状态」引申出「被置于其中、难以改变的状况」，再进一步具体化为糟糕的困境。

senses.title: A dilemma with no easy answer
senses.definition: a choice in which every option brings harm or loss
senses.definitionCN: 每一种选择都会带来损害或损失的两难选择
senses.example: The council faced the predicament of raising taxes or cutting services.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会面临两难：要么加税，要么削减服务。
senses.why: When a declared condition offers no good way out, the situation turns into a dilemma, a branch with no safe path.
senses.whyCN: 当一个既定状况里没有好出路时，它就成了两难：每条岔路都不安全，这正是困境的极端形态。

senses.title: A moral or ethical trouble
senses.definition: an awkward position caused by conflicting moral duties or obligations
senses.definitionCN: 由相互冲突的道德义务造成的尴尬处境
senses.example: Doctors often face the moral predicament of telling the whole truth.
senses.exampleCN: 医生常常面临该如何说出全部真相的道德困境。
senses.why: The idea of a condition announced before others suits moral life, where duty and honesty may pull in opposite directions.
senses.whyCN: 「在众人面前被宣告的状态」很适合道德生活：责任与诚实可能彼此拉扯，人便卡在中间难以取舍。

senses.title: A formal classification in logic
senses.definition: one of the classes or categories in which things are arranged in logic
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑学中事物被归入的类别或范畴
senses.example: Old logic books divide terms into predicaments such as substance and quality.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的逻辑学著作把术语分为实体、性质这样的类目。
senses.why: In Aristotelian logic a predicament is a category assigned to a subject, a use preserved in English and later eclipsed by the everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 在亚里士多德逻辑学里，predicament 指「归属于某个主词的范畴」；这一用法进入英语后被日常义项盖过，但词形仍保留着「被归入某类」的骨架。

intro.en: Predicament goes back to Latin praedicamentum, something declared, which in medieval logic named a category, and only later came to mean a difficult situation.
intro.cn: predicament 源于拉丁语 praedicamentum（被宣告之物），中世纪逻辑学用它指「范畴」，直到较晚时期才表示「困境、窘境」。

items.en: Praedicare means to proclaim, to declare publicly, from prae, before, and dicare, to make known.
items.cn: praedicare 意为宣告、公开宣称，由 prae（在前）与 dicare（使知晓）构成。

items.en: Praedicamentum names what is asserted of a subject, and in Aristotle commentaries it renders the Greek word for category.
items.cn: praedicamentum 指「关于某个主词所断言的东西」，在亚里士多德评注中用来对译希腊语的「范畴」。

items.en: Medieval logic treats predicaments as the ten categories of being, from substance to posture.
items.cn: 中世纪逻辑学把 predicament 视为存在的十大范畴，从实体一直到姿态。

items.en: Middle English borrows the word through Old French and uses it for a logical category.
items.cn: 中古英语经古法语借入该词，最初用作逻辑学上的「范畴」。

items.en: By this period the word widens to mean a condition or state in which someone is placed.
items.cn: 到这一时期，词义扩展为「某人被置于其中的状况或状态」。

items.en: Modern English fixes the everyday sense of an awkward and hard situation, while the logic sense survives mainly in specialist writing.
items.cn: 现代英语把「尴尬难办的处境」定为日常义项，逻辑学义项则主要留在专业文献里。

note.en: Predicament is a state one is placed in against one will, so it sits close to plight and dilemma, and looks like words sharing the Latin root praedicare.
note.cn: predicament 指被人置于其中、身不由己的状况，因此与 plight、dilemma 相邻；形近词则共用拉丁语 praedicare 的词根。

entries.definition: the part of a sentence that says something about the subject
entries.definitionCN: 谓语；述语，与 predicament 同出拉丁语 praedicare，词义已完全不同

entries.definition: to give a religious talk or urge people to act well
entries.definitionCN: 布道；说教，同源但拼写已缩短，是判别词根的线索

entries.definition: relating to the part of a sentence that follows a linking verb
entries.definitionCN: 表语的；谓述的，是同源家族的形容词

entries.definition: a dangerous or unhappy situation
entries.definitionCN: 困境；苦境，与 predicament 最近，但更强调危险与不幸

entries.definition: a choice between two equally unwelcome options
entries.definitionCN: 两难境地，强调必须二选一时两头都难

entries.definition: a state of confusion about what to do
entries.definitionCN: 窘境；困惑，强调不知道该怎么办

normalIntro.en: Predicament shares its root with preach and predicate: something publicly declared. A declared state you cannot change becomes a predicament.
normalIntro.cn: predicament 与 preach、predicate 同根，本义是「被公开宣告之物」；一旦这个被宣告的状态无法更改，就成了困境。

normal.en: The Latin root prae means before, and dicare means to make known, so to declare is to say something out in front of others.
normal.cn: 拉丁语词根 prae 表示「在前」，dicare 表示「使知晓」，所以「宣告」就是把事情摆到众人面前说出来。

normal.en: In a predicament the situation has already been declared and you can no longer argue it away.
normal.cn: 身处 predicament 时，处境已经被「宣告」出来，你再怎么争辩也改不了。

normal.en: Predicate, predicative, and predicament all come from one declared thing, though only predicament turned into a bad situation.
normal.cn: predicate、predicative 与 predicament 都来自「被宣告之物」，只有 predicament 演化成了糟糕的处境。

normal.en: Learn the frame in a predicament and get into a predicament; they show that the word is always a place you are inside.
normal.cn: 记住 in a predicament 和 get into a predicament 这两个框架，能看出这个词永远指你「身在其中」的处境。

normal.en: Keep predicament for serious trouble in writing and speech; plight is its closer everyday twin, while dilemma adds the idea of a choice.
normal.cn: predicament 用于书面和口语中较为严重的麻烦；plight 更贴近日常，而 dilemma 额外含有「必须做选择」的意思。

abstract.en: Picture a room where three walls have slid shut and the fourth is a window you cannot open.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间，三面墙已经合拢，第四面是一扇打不开的窗。

abstract.en: Imagine a scale with two trays, both loaded with something you would rather not take.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，两个托盘里都放着你不想要的东西。

abstract.en: Think of a judge reading out a ruling about your life, and everyone in the court turning to look at you.
abstract.cn: 想象法官当庭宣读一项关于你生活的判决，全场的人都转头看你。

examples.en: The refugees faced a desperate predicament, with no food and no papers.
examples.cn: 难民们陷入绝望的困境，既没有食物，也没有证件。

examples.en: How did you get into such a predicament?
examples.cn: 你怎么会陷入这样的窘境？

examples.en: Her predicament was that she had to choose between her career and her family.
examples.cn: 她的困境在于必须在事业和家庭之间做出选择。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑进去可闷头」——一头扑进去，结果闷在里面出不来，就是在困境里打转；这只是声音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 prae（在前）+ dicare（宣称、使知晓）→ praedicare（宣告）→ 晚期拉丁语 praedicamentum（被断言之物、范畴）→ 经古法语进入英语 predicament，核心义「被公开宣定、难以更改的状况」。

sensesIntro.en: Predicament starts as a declared category, becomes a condition one is placed in, then narrows to a hard situation, a forced choice, and a moral trouble.
sensesIntro.cn: predicament 最初指被宣告的「范畴」，后来指人被置于其中的状态，再收窄为难办的处境、被迫的二选一，以及道德上的尴尬处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person shut in by three walls, with one narrow way out they cannot see.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人被三面墙围住，只剩一条窄路，却看不见出口。

branches.en: A hard situation is the everyday sense, the condition turned unpleasant.
branches.cn: 难办的处境是最常用义项，即「被置于其中的状况」变得糟糕。

branches.en: A dilemma is the same trap viewed as a forced choice.
branches.cn: 两难是同一座陷阱的另一面：必须做出选择。

branches.en: A moral predicament pushes the trap inside, into duty and conscience.
branches.cn: 道德困境把陷阱移入内心，落在责任与良心上。

branches.en: The logical category is the oldest layer, kept only in specialist writing.
branches.cn: 逻辑学上的「范畴」是最古老的一层，只在专业文献中保留。

branches.en: Everyday predicaments often hide a choice between two losses, which is why people speak of being stuck.
branches.cn: 日常困境常常暗含「两种损失选其一」的选择，所以人们常说「卡住了」。

intro.en: Predicament comes from a Latin verb of declaring, and the family around it includes preach, predicate, and predicative.
intro.cn: predicament 来自一个表示「宣告」的拉丁语动词，围绕它构成的词族包括 preach、predicate 与 predicative。

latinIntro.en: Latin prae means before, dicare means to make known, and praedicare means to proclaim; praedicamentum is the thing proclaimed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prae 意为「在前」，dicare 意为「使知晓」，praedicare 意为「宣告」，praedicamentum 则是「被宣告之物」。

items.example: The prefix prae- gives the sense of speaking out in front.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 prae- 给出「在众人面前说出」的意味。

items.example: Dicare is the declaring element inside the word.
items.exampleCN: dicare 是词中「宣告」的那部分。

items.example: Praedicare is the direct ancestor of the English word.
items.exampleCN: praedicare 是英语本词的直接祖先。

items.meaning: that which is asserted, a category
items.example: Praedicamentum carries the category sense into medieval learning.
items.exampleCN: praedicamentum 把「范畴」义带入中世纪学术。

items.example: Preach is a shortened cousin from the same Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: preach 是来自同一拉丁动词的缩略近亲。

items.meaning: the part of a sentence that states something about the subject
items.example: Predicate keeps the grammar sense of something stated.
items.exampleCN: predicate 保留了「被述说的东西」这一语法义。

items.meaning: relating to what is stated about a subject
items.example: Predicative describes a position after a linking verb.
items.exampleCN: predicative 描述系动词之后的位置。

items.example: Predetermined is a look-alike built with pre-, a different Latin prefix.
items.exampleCN: predetermined 是形近词，它用 pre- 构成，前缀另有来源。

definition_zh: 可预测性；可预见性；规律性；可预知的程度
definition_en: the quality of being able to be known or stated in advance with confidence
core_image: 日历上一排排相同的格子：每天都会在同一个时间打开同一扇门
scene: 老式火车站里，报站员每天在同一分钟吹哨，乘客闭着眼也知道下一步该去哪。Commuters on the old line rely on the predictability of the timetable and never check it twice.
sceneCN: 这里 predictability 是「可预见性」（第 1 个义项：事物能被事先料到）；句意：老线路上的通勤者信赖时刻表的可预见性，从不查看第二遍。

pos.zh: 可预测性；可预见性；规律性

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀 -ability 后的基础动词，义为「预言；预测」
predict + -able，意为「可预测的」，再加 -ity 即成名词 predictability
predict + -ive，意为「预测性的；有预见作用的」，强调具备预言功能
predictable + -ly，意为「不出所料地」，常用来表示结果毫无悬念
加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不可预测性」，是本词最常用的对照词

senses.title: The quality of being expected in advance
senses.definition: the quality of something that can be known or forecast before it happens
senses.definitionCN: 事物在发生之前就能被知道或预报的性质
senses.example: Meteorologists are working to improve the predictability of storms.
senses.exampleCN: 气象学家正致力于提高风暴的可预测性。
senses.why: The base verb pre-dictare combines pre, before, with dictare, to say, so whatever can be said before it happens has predictability.
senses.whyCN: 基础动词 pre-dictare 由 pre（在前）与 dictare（说）组成，凡是能「事先被说出来」的事物就具有可预测性。

senses.title: Reliability through steady repetition
senses.definition: the quality of following a steady pattern that does not surprise
senses.definitionCN: 遵循稳定模式、不会出人意料的性质
senses.example: Children need the predictability of regular meals and bedtimes.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子需要有规律的用餐和就寝时间带来的稳定感。
senses.why: When a pattern repeats exactly, each new round can be said beforehand, so meaning drifts from what can be known to the routine that makes it knowable.
senses.whyCN: 当某种模式精确地重复时，每一轮都能被事先说出，于是词义从「能被预知」转向「产生预知的规律本身」。

senses.title: Dull sameness that invites criticism
senses.definition: a negative quality of being too routine, so that nothing surprises or excites
senses.definitionCN: 过于程式化、毫无惊喜的可预测特质，带贬义
senses.example: Critics complained about the predictability of the film ending.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家抱怨这部电影的结局一成不变。
senses.why: What can be guessed too easily stops being comfort and becomes monotony, so the neutral quality takes on a disapproving tone.
senses.whyCN: 太容易猜到的事物不再让人安心，反而变成乏味单调，于是这个中性特质染上了批评色彩。

senses.title: A scientific measure of forecast accuracy
senses.definition: in science, the measurable degree to which a system can be forecast
senses.definitionCN: 科学上指一个系统能够被预报的可测量程度
senses.example: Chaos theory limits the predictability of long term weather forecasts.
senses.exampleCN: 混沌理论限制了长期天气预报的可预报程度。
senses.why: Adding the abstract noun suffix turns the everyday quality into a measurable quantity, which weather science and chaos theory need.
senses.whyCN: 加上抽象名词后缀后，日常的「可预见」变成可度量的量，这正是天气科学与混沌理论所需要的。

senses.title: The extent to which a person can be read
senses.definition: the degree to which a person acts in ways others can foresee
senses.definitionCN: 一个人行为被他人预先料到的程度
senses.example: His predictability made him easy to work with but hard to admire.
senses.exampleCN: 他的可捉摸让他易于共事，却难以令人钦佩。
senses.why: Applied to people, the quality becomes a description of character, the sense in which someone always reacts the same way.
senses.whyCN: 用于人时，这个特质就变成性格描述：某人总是以同样的方式反应，让人一眼看穿。

intro.en: Predictability is built from pre- and Latin dicere, to say, plus the noun suffix -ability, so at root it means the capacity to be said beforehand.
intro.cn: predictability 由前缀 pre-、拉丁语 dicere（说）与名词后缀 -ability 组成，词根义就是「能被事先说出来的能力」。

items.en: Dicere means to say, and its frequentative dicare means to keep saying or declare.
items.cn: dicere 意为「说」，其反复态 dicare 意为「反复说、声明」。

items.en: Praedicare, with prae, before, means to proclaim or foretell.
items.cn: praedicare 加上前缀 prae（在前），意为事先宣称或预告。

items.en: English forms the verb predict, meaning to say that something will happen.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪构成动词 predict，意为预言某事将会发生。

items.en: Predictable appears as the adjective with the suffix -able, and predictability follows from it.
items.cn: 带后缀 -able 的形容词 predictable 出现，名词 predictability 由它派生而来。

items.en: Predictability spreads into weather science, economics, and business planning as a measure of reliability.
items.cn: 现代英语中 predictability 进入气象学、经济学与商业规划，成为衡量可靠性的术语。

note.en: Predictability belongs to a Latin word family that says things in advance, and to the same meaning group as foreknowledge and consistency.
note.cn: predictability 属于「事先说出」的拉丁词族，与 foreknowledge、consistency 同属一个意义群。

entries.definition: to say what will happen in the future
entries.definitionCN: 预言；预测，是本词的基础动词

entries.definition: able to be known in advance
entries.definitionCN: 可预见的，加 -ity 即是本词

entries.definition: a person who held a job before someone else
entries.definitionCN: 前任，与 predictability 只是都以 pre- 开头，词根其实不同

entries.definition: knowledge of what will happen in advance
entries.definitionCN: 预知；预先知道，强调已知的结果而非可被知道的性质

entries.definition: the quality of always behaving in the same way
entries.definitionCN: 一致性，与本词第 2 个义项最接近

entries.definition: the quality of occurring at even intervals
entries.definitionCN: 规律性，侧重时间间隔上的稳定

entries.definition: the quality of being impossible to foresee
entries.definitionCN: 不可预测性，是本词的直接反义词

normalIntro.en: Break the word open: pre means before, dict means say, and ability means power to, so predictability is the power of something to be said before it happens.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆开：pre 表「在前」，dict 表「说」，ability 表「……的能力」，所以 predictability 就是「某事物能被事先说出的能力」。

normal.en: Dict in predictability is the same dict in dictionary and dictate, a root about saying and declaring.
normal.cn: predictability 里的 dict 与 dictionary、dictate 同根，都与「说、宣告」有关。

normal.en: The suffix -ability turns an adjective into a noun quality, as in ability and stability.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ability 把形容词变成名词性质，和 ability、stability 是同一套构词法。

normal.en: Unpredictability is the natural partner, so learn the pair together and you own both sides.
normal.cn: unpredictability 是天然的对偶词，成对记下这两个词就能掌握正反两面。

normal.en: Boring predictability is a common set phrase that shows the word can be used as a criticism.
normal.cn: boring predictability 是常见搭配，说明本词也能当批评用。

normal.en: In science the word is countable and specific, as in the predictability of a system, a measurable property rather than a vague feeling.
normal.cn: 科学语境里本词具体而可度量，如 the predictability of a system，是可测性质而不是模糊感觉。

abstract.en: Picture a row of identical calendar squares, each one holding the same appointment.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上一排一模一样的格子，每一格都写着同一个约会。

abstract.en: Imagine a clock that people trust so much they no longer glance at it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只大家如此信任的钟，以至于没人再去看它。

abstract.en: Think of a film whose final scene you can recite before it plays.
abstract.cn: 想象一部电影，它的最后一幕在播放前你就能背出来。

examples.en: Investors prize predictability above dramatic growth.
examples.cn: 投资者看重可预测性胜过戏剧性的增长。

examples.en: The predictability of the seasons shapes farming practice across the region.
examples.cn: 季节的规律性塑造了这一地区的农耕方式。

examples.en: She was tired of the dull predictability of her working days.
examples.cn: 她厌倦了工作日里那一成不变的乏味。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑雷地克特」——名字叫得再难记，第二天照样在同一时间出现，正因为可预测；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pre-（在前）+ dicere（说）→ predict（预言）+ 后缀 -able → predictable（可预见的）+ 后缀 -ity → predictability，核心义「能被事先说出来、因而能够被信赖」。

sensesIntro.en: Predictability begins as the fact of being foreseeable, grows into the routine that makes foresight possible, and can sour into monotony or sharpen into a measured quantity.
sensesIntro.cn: predictability 起初指「能被预见」这一事实，继而指让预见成为可能的规律，之后既可贬为单调乏味，也可精确为可度量的科研指标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of identical calendar squares, each with the same appointment.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上一排相同的格子，每格都是同一个约会。

branches.en: Being foreseeable is the literal and general sense of the word.
branches.cn: 能被预见是本词最字面、最概括的义项。

branches.en: The steady pattern is what produces foresight in daily life.
branches.cn: 稳定模式正是日常生活中产生预见力的来源。

branches.en: Pushed too far, the same pattern becomes dull monotony.
branches.cn: 稳定模式走到极端，就成了乏味的单调。

branches.en: Science measures the quality rather than merely describing it.
branches.cn: 科学语境把这种性质量化，而不只是描述。

branches.en: Applied to people, the quality reads as character and is judged good or bad.
branches.cn: 用于人时，这种性质被读成性格，并被褒贬评判。

intro.en: Predictability is a transparent compound of a Latin prefix, a Latin root, and an English noun suffix, with the words predict and predictable as its nearest family.
intro.cn: predictability 由拉丁前缀、拉丁词根与英语名词后缀透明组合而成，最近的家庭成员是 predict 与 predictable。

latinIntro.en: Latin dicere means to say and dicare means to declare; with pre, before, they produce the verb predict.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dicere 意为「说」，dicare 意为「宣告」，加上 pre（在前）就构成动词 predict。

items.example: The prefix pre- puts the saying before the event.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pre- 把这个「说」放在事件之前。

items.example: Dicere is the root of speaking inside the word.
items.exampleCN: dicere 是词中表示「说」的词根。

items.example: The suffix -able turns predict into predictable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 把 predict 变成 predictable。

items.example: The suffix -ability turns the adjective into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ability 把形容词变回名词。

items.meaning: a book that lists the meanings of words
items.example: Dictionary shares the saying root dict.
items.exampleCN: dictionary 共用表示「说」的词根 dict。

items.meaning: to say words for someone to write down
items.example: Dictate shows the root saying out loud.
items.exampleCN: dictate 体现词根「大声说」的一面。

items.meaning: to say the opposite of something
items.example: Contradict uses contra, against, plus the same root.
items.exampleCN: contradict 用 contra（相反）加上同一词根。

items.meaning: the quality of being impossible to foresee
items.example: The prefix un- flips the meaning to its opposite.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 把词义翻转成反面。

items.example: The suffix -ive suggests an active power of foretelling.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 暗示一种主动的预言能力。

definition_zh: 使预先倾向于；使易患；使先有偏见；预先安排
definition_en: to make someone or something likely to think, feel, or behave in a particular way
core_image: 在天平还没开始称之前，一端已经悄悄压上了砝码
scene: 医生看着体检报告，提醒中年病人要注意体重和血压。Smoking and a family history of the illness predispose many people to heart disease.
sceneCN: 这里 predispose 是「使易患」（第 2 个义项：使身体容易得某种病）；句意：吸烟和家族病史使许多人容易患上心脏病。

collocations.zh: 使儿童易于产生攻击性

derivatives.zh: predispose + 后缀 -ition 构成的名词，义为「倾向；易感性；先入之见」
过去分词作形容词，义为「有倾向的；易感的」，常与 be 连用
现在分词作形容词，多见于医学语境，义为「易感性的；诱发性的」
去掉前缀 pre- 后的基础动词，义为「处置；使倾向于」

senses.title: To make someone likely to act in a certain way
senses.definition: to make a person more likely to think, feel, or behave in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 使某人在思考、感受或行为上更可能朝某个方向发展
senses.example: Constant praise predisposed the child to enjoy reading aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 不断的表扬使这个孩子倾向于喜欢大声朗读。
senses.why: Pre- places the action beforehand and dispose arranges things, so predispose means to set the mind in order before the moment arrives.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 pre- 把动作放到「之前」，dispose 本是「安排、安置」，合起来就是在事情发生之前先把心理摆好方向。

senses.title: To make a body more liable to illness
senses.definition: to make someone more likely to become ill with a particular disease
senses.definitionCN: 使某人更容易患上某种疾病
senses.example: A weak immune system predisposes patients to infection.
senses.exampleCN: 免疫系统薄弱使病人容易感染。
senses.why: Medicine uses the same before-arranged idea for the body, where hereditary or lifestyle factors tilt an organism towards disease.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这种「事先摆好」的思路用在身体上：遗传或生活方式因素让机体在疾病出现前就偏向一侧。

senses.title: To give someone a bias in advance
senses.definition: to lead someone to judge something unfairly before knowing the facts
senses.definitionCN: 使某人在了解事实之前就形成不公平的判断
senses.example: The early news reports predisposed the jury against the defendant.
senses.exampleCN: 早期的新闻报道使陪审团对被告产生了先入之见。
senses.why: If the mind is arranged in advance, new evidence no longer enters freely, and this unbalance shows up as prejudice.
senses.whyCN: 若心思已提前摆好方向，新证据就难以自由进入，这种天平倾斜就表现为偏见。

senses.title: To set something up beforehand
senses.definition: to arrange or set in readiness in advance
senses.definitionCN: 事先把某事安排好或准备好
senses.example: The programme was predisposed to fail from the first day.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目从第一天起就注定要失败。
senses.why: The literal sense of disposing before the fact survives alongside the psychological one, mostly in formal or ironic usage.
senses.whyCN: 「在事实之前就安排好」的字面义与心理义并存，多见于正式或略带反讽的表达。

intro.en: Predispose joins the Latin prefix pre, before, to the verb dispose from Latin disponere, to arrange, and was modelled on French predisposer in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: predispose 由拉丁语前缀 pre（在前）与动词 dispose（源于拉丁语 disponere「安排」）结合而成，一般认为仿照十七世纪法语 predisposer 构成。

items.en: Disponere means to put in order, from dis-, apart, and ponere, to place.
items.cn: disponere 意为「安排、布置」，由 dis-（分开）与 ponere（放置）构成。

items.en: Old French disposer gives English the verb dispose, carrying the arranging sense.
items.cn: 古法语 disposer 把「安排」义带入英语，形成动词 dispose。

items.en: French forms predisposer by adding pre to disposer, producing the idea of arranging in advance.
items.cn: 法语在 disposer 前加 pre 构成 predisposer，产生「事先安排」的含义。

items.en: English takes up predispose, at first meaning to set in readiness beforehand.
items.cn: 英语借入 predispose，早期意为「预先布置妥当」。

items.en: The word moves from objects to minds and bodies, and becomes common in medicine and moral writing.
items.cn: 该词从物品转向心理与身体，开始广泛出现在医学与道德论述中。

items.en: Modern dictionaries list both the psychological and the medical uses, and predisposition is the standard noun.
items.cn: 现代词典并列收录心理学与医学两方面的用法，其标准名词形式为 predisposition。

note.en: Predispose keeps the pre of before and the Latin root that also gives pose and position, so it looks like a family of posing words and sits near incline and prone in meaning.
note.cn: predispose 保留了表示「在前」的 pre 以及同出 pose、position 的拉丁词根，形近上是一组「放置」词，意义则与 incline、prone 相邻。

entries.definition: a natural tendency to behave or be affected in a certain way
entries.definitionCN: 倾向；易感性，是本词最直接的名词形式

entries.definition: to arrange or to get rid of
entries.definitionCN: 处置；使倾向于，去掉 pre- 即为本词基础

entries.definition: to force something on others
entries.definitionCN: 强加；征收，前缀不同，同出拉丁语 ponere「放置」

entries.definition: to make someone willing to do or believe something
entries.definitionCN: 使倾向于，语气比 predispose 弱，未必指事先形成

entries.definition: likely to be affected by something bad
entries.definitionCN: 易于……的，侧重后果而非内在倾向

entries.definition: likely to suffer from or do something bad
entries.definitionCN: 易于（受害或犯错的），常后接 to，与第 2 个义项对应

normalIntro.en: Read predispose as pre plus dispose: to dispose of the mind or body means to arrange it, so predispose is to arrange it before anything happens.
normalIntro.cn: 把 predispose 读成 pre 加 dispose：dispose 是「安排、布置」，那么 predispose 就是在任何事情发生之前先安排好。

normal.en: The prefix pre- marks everything as happening early, which is why the word always suggests a cause that works in advance.
normal.cn: 前缀 pre- 把所有动作都标成「提前发生」，所以这个词总暗示某种起作用的原因出现在事件之前。

normal.en: Dispose and position share Latin ponere, to place, so a predisposition is a placing of the mind or body on one side.
normal.cn: dispose 与 position 同为拉丁语 ponere（放置）所生，所以 predisposition 就是把心智或身体放到一侧。

normal.en: The noun predisposition is the standard partner, used in medicine for a tendency to a disease.
normal.cn: 名词 predisposition 是标准搭档，医学上指对某种疾病的易感倾向。

normal.en: Genetically predisposed is the set phrase that appears most often in health writing.
normal.cn: genetically predisposed 是健康类文章里最常见的固定搭配。

normal.en: Predispose is a verb, so read it with its objects: predispose someone to something, or be predisposed to do something.
normal.cn: predispose 是动词，要连同宾语一起记：predispose someone to something 或 be predisposed to do something。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that is secretly weighted on one side before anyone steps onto it.
abstract.cn: 想象一台天平，还没人站上去，一端就被悄悄压上了砝码。

abstract.en: Imagine a seed already pointing the way a tree will lean years before it grows.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗种子在长成之前就已经决定了树将来往哪边倾斜。

abstract.en: Think of a jury who read the newspaper headlines before the trial began.
abstract.cn: 想象陪审团在开庭前先读了报纸头条。

examples.en: His upbringing predisposed him to distrust strangers.
examples.cn: 他的成长经历使他倾向于不信任陌生人。

examples.en: Certain genes predispose people to the disease.
examples.cn: 某些基因会让人易患这种疾病。

examples.en: Fatigue can predispose drivers to serious mistakes.
examples.cn: 疲劳会使司机容易犯下严重错误。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑雷迪斯剖」——天平还没开始称，一端就已经压上砝码，自然偏向一边；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pre-（在前）+ dis-（分开）+ ponere（放置）→ disponere（安排）→ 法语 predisposer → 英语 predispose，核心义「事发之前先把心思或身体摆向一侧」。

sensesIntro.en: Predispose always places something in advance: first the mind, then the body, then judgement, and finally any arrangement made before it happens.
sensesIntro.cn: predispose 始终是「提前摆放」：先摆心智，再摆身体，然后是判断力，最后泛指任何事先做出的安排。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale already weighted on one side before anything is put on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平在开始称重之前，一端已被压上砝码。

branches.en: Tilting the mind towards a response is the general, everyday sense.
branches.cn: 把心智倾向某种反应，是本词最概括的日常义项。

branches.en: Tilting the body towards disease is the medical extension.
branches.cn: 把身体倾向疾病，是医学上的延伸义项。

branches.en: Tilting judgement before the facts arrive is the bias sense.
branches.cn: 事实到来前就倾动判断，就是偏见义项。

branches.en: Arranging anything beforehand keeps the original literal sense alive.
branches.cn: 任何预先安排都保留着最原始的字面义。

branches.en: Both habit and heredity work the same way, by lightening one side of the scale long before the event.
branches.cn: 习惯与遗传的作用方式相同：在事情发生很久以前就把天平的一边压轻。

intro.en: Predispose stacks two Latin prefixes on a Latin root of placing, and its relatives include dispose, disposition, and predisposition.
intro.cn: predispose 在拉丁语「放置」词根上叠了两个前缀，家族成员包括 dispose、disposition 与 predisposition。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere means to place, and its compound disponere means to arrange; the prefix pre marks the arranging as happening beforehand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ponere 意为「放置」，其复合词 disponere 意为「安排」；前缀 pre 则标明这种安排发生在事先。

items.example: The prefix pre- gives the word its early timing.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pre- 赋予本词「时间在前」的含义。

items.example: Inside dispose the prefix dis- suggests spreading things out.
items.exampleCN: 在 dispose 里，前缀 dis- 暗示把东西分散摆开。

items.example: Ponere is the placing root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: ponere 是整个家族的「放置」词根。

items.meaning: to arrange, to set in order
items.example: Disponere is the Latin source of dispose.
items.exampleCN: disponere 是 dispose 的拉丁语来源。

items.meaning: to arrange or to get rid of
items.example: Dispose is the base verb once the pre- is removed.
items.exampleCN: 去掉 pre- 之后，dispose 就是基础动词。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或状态的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ition builds predisposition from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ition 把动词变成 predisposition。

items.example: Predisposition is the noun of the verb predispose.
items.exampleCN: predisposition 是 predispose 的名词形式。

items.example: Disposition keeps the arranging sense without the prefix.
items.exampleCN: disposition 不带前缀，仍保留「安排」的意味。

items.meaning: to uncover or to make known
items.example: Expose uses the same root with the prefix ex-, out.
items.exampleCN: expose 用同一词根配合前缀 ex-（向外）。

items.example: Impose and predispose share the placing root.
items.exampleCN: impose 与 predispose 共用「放置」词根。

definition_zh: 占优势；占多数；支配；占上风
definition_en: to be the most powerful, most common, or strongest part of something
core_image: 一群人围坐，一个人高高坐镇，其余都听他
scene: 在村口的老祠堂里开议事会，大家争来争去，最后是由长辈们说了算。At the village meeting, the opinions of the elders predominate over all the others.
sceneCN: 这里 predominate 是「占优势、占支配地位」，对应第 1 个义项：在某种局面中成为最强大的力量；句意：在村里的议事会上，长辈们的意见压倒了其他所有人的意见。

derivatives.zh: predominate 去动词词尾加名词后缀 -ance，义为「主导地位；多数」
加形容词后缀 -ant，义为「占主导的；主要的」
在形容词后加 -ly，义为「主要地；大多地」
现在分词作形容词，义为「占优势的」

senses.title: To be the strongest force
senses.definition: to be the most powerful or important force in a situation or group
senses.definitionCN: 在某种局面或群体中成为最强大、最重要的力量
senses.example: In that committee, a few senior members predominate.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个委员会里，几位资深成员占支配地位。
senses.why: The prefix pre- means before and root dominari means to rule, so what predominates rules ahead of everything else.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 pre- 表示「在前」，词根 dominari 表示「统治」，于是占优势就是在其他力量之前说了算。

senses.title: To be the most common
senses.definition: to form the largest part or the greatest number of something
senses.definitionCN: 构成某事物的最大部分或最大数量
senses.example: Small family farms predominate in this valley.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个山谷里，小型家庭农场占多数。
senses.why: A majority outvotes everything else in size, so the same ruling image turns into counting and numbers.
senses.whyCN: 多数在数量上压过其余一切，因此「说了算」的画面自然转成了数数。

senses.title: To win out over another effect
senses.definition: to become stronger than another quality, feeling, or influence
senses.definitionCN: 变得比另一种性质、情感或影响力更强
senses.example: Curiosity eventually predominated over his fear.
senses.exampleCN: 好奇心最终战胜了他的恐惧。
senses.why: When two forces meet, the ruling one sits above its rival, so the verb also means winning out.
senses.whyCN: 两种力量相遇时，说了算的一方坐在对手之上，所以这个词也有压过对方的意思。

senses.title: To point strongly toward a view
senses.definition: to be the main evidence or the main reason that leads someone to a conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 成为使某人得出某种结论的主要证据或主要理由
senses.example: The evidence predominates in favour of the new plan.
senses.exampleCN: 证据明显倾向于支持这项新计划。
senses.why: If one force rules the scene, an observer naturally forms a judgement along it, so the word covers swaying opinion.
senses.whyCN: 若一种力量主导了整个场面，观察者自然会顺着它作判断，于是这个词也涵盖了左右看法。

senses.title: The predominant quality
senses.definition: the state or quality of being the chief or leading one
senses.definitionCN: 处于首要或领先地位的状态或性质
senses.example: The predominance of grey stone gives the old town a quiet tone.
senses.exampleCN: 灰石的主导地位给这座古镇一种安静的气质。
senses.why: The abstract noun names the ruling itself, turning the seated image into a lasting quality of a place or period.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式命名的是「统治」这件事本身，把坐镇的画面变成地方或时代的持久特征。

senses.title: Especially common or typical
senses.definition: described as the most common kind in a place or period
senses.definitionCN: 被描述为某地或某时期最常见的类型
senses.example: Rice is the predominant crop along the southern coast.
senses.exampleCN: 水稻是南部沿海最主要的作物。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the before ruling image and applies it to a crop or a breed so common that it sets the standard.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了「在前统治」的画面，用来形容一种常见到成为标准的作物或品种。

senses.title: The tone that wins the frame
senses.definition: the colour or tone that takes up the largest part of a picture
senses.definitionCN: 在画面中占据最大面积的颜色或基调
senses.example: Red predominates in the canvas of the artist.
senses.exampleCN: 在这位画家的画布上，红色占主导。
senses.why: In painting the ruling force is the largest block of colour, so the verb also describes a colour that wins the frame.
senses.whyCN: 在绘画里，起统治作用的往往是面积最大的色块，于是这个词也能描述统治画面的颜色。

intro.en: Predominate combines the Latin prefix prae-, meaning before, with dominari, to rule, so it literally means to rule ahead of the rest.
intro.cn: predominate 由拉丁语前缀 prae-（在前）与 dominari（统治）合成，字面就是「抢在别人前面做主」。

items.en: Dominari means to be master of or to rule, a verb built on dominus, lord.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dominari 意为做主人或统治，是从 dominus（主人）构成的动词。

items.en: Late Latin adds the prefix prae-, giving praedominari, to rule before others.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语加上前缀 prae-，构成 praedominari，意为比别人先行做主。

items.en: Scholastic and legal writings use predominari for what holds the upper hand.
items.cn: 中世纪的经院与法律文献用 predominari 表示居于上风的事物。

items.en: English borrows the verb as predominate, following French terminology.
items.cn: 英语借入该动词写成 predominate，术语路径受法语影响。

items.en: The adjective predominant above all means the most common or most frequent.
items.cn: 到了近代，形容词 predominant 与副词 predominantly 主要表示最常见、最普遍。

items.en: Today the verb is neutral, describing majorities in science, politics, and daily speech.
items.cn: 今天这个动词是中性的，用来描述科学、政治和日常语言中占多数的情况。

note.en: Predominate sits in the same ruling family as dominate and predominant, and shares its meaning field with prevail and outnumber.
note.cn: predominate 与 dominate、predominant 属于同一个「统治」词族，意义上又和 prevail、outnumber 相邻。

entries.definition: most common or most powerful
entries.definitionCN: 最常见或最强大的；占主导的

entries.definition: the state of being dominant
mainly
to control something strongly
to be the strongest or most common
to be more in number than

normalIntro.en: Predominate is a ruling picture: pre- puts a person in front, and dominari puts them in charge.
normalIntro.cn: predominate 是一幅做主的画面：pre- 把人放到前面，dominari 让人说了算。

normal.en: Think of dominate, which is simply to rule, and pre- which adds the sense of being first.
normal.cn: 先想 dominate（统治），再加 pre-（在前），就是抢先统治。

normal.en: Predominate in a group means to be the largest or most powerful part of it.
normal.cn: predominate in 某个群体，就是成为其中最大或最强的那部分。

normal.en: The adverb predominantly is very common in IELTS writing, as in predominantly residential.
normal.cn: 副词 predominantly 在雅思写作里很常见，比如 predominantly residential。

normal.en: Pair the verb with over when two forces compete, as in reason predominates over emotion.
normal.cn: 两种力量较量时用 over 搭配，例如 reason predominates over emotion。

normal.en: Remember the noun predominance for the share or status of what dominates.
normal.cn: 记住名词 predominance，表示主导者的份额或地位。

abstract.en: Imagine a scale where one pan sits low and heavy, pulling everything toward it.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆秤，一边的秤盘沉下去、压得很重，把一切都拉向它。

abstract.en: Imagine a crowd of mixed colours in which one bright hue takes up most of the view.
abstract.cn: 想象一团杂色的染料里，一种亮色占满了大半个画面。

abstract.en: Imagine a noisy debate where one voice finally rises above all the others.
abstract.cn: 想象一场吵闹的辩论，最后有一个声音盖过了所有人。

examples.en: Wheat predominates in the northern fields.
examples.cn: 北方田野里小麦占多数。

examples.en: In this industry, small firms predominate.
examples.cn: 在这个行业里，小公司占主导地位。

examples.en: Their village economy is still predominantly agricultural.
examples.cn: 他们的村庄经济仍然以农业为主。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞domin吃」——普瑞这个大老板先把饭吃了，别人只能看着，谐音联想他凡事占先、占上风；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ dominari（统治，来自 dominus「主人」）→ 晚期拉丁语 praedominari → 英语 predominate，核心义「抢先做主、占上风」。

sensesIntro.en: Predominate starts as a picture of one force ruling over others, then spreads to counting, competing feelings, evidence, abstract nouns, adjectives, and even colour.
sensesIntro.cn: predominate 先是一幅「一种力量压过其余」的画面，再从力量扩展到数量、相互竞争的情感、证据、名词状态、形容词以及颜色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one figure seated above the rest, ruling the room.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人高坐于众人之上，统领全场。

branches.en: Being the strongest force is the earliest everyday sense.
branches.cn: 成为最强的力量是最早、最日常的义项。

branches.en: Being the greatest number is the counting extension.
branches.cn: 成为最大的数量是向计数延伸出的义项。

branches.en: Winning out over a rival shows the same force in motion.
branches.cn: 压过对手体现的是同一个「力量」在运动中的样子。

branches.en: Swaying a judgement is an extension from force to evidence.
branches.cn: 左右判断是从力量延伸到证据领域。

branches.en: The abstract noun, the adjective, and the colour sense all freeze the ruling image.
branches.cn: 名词、形容词与颜色义项都是把「做主」的画面定格下来。

intro.en: English builds a small ruling family around the Latin root dominus: dominate, predominant, predominance, and predominantly.
intro.cn: 英语围绕拉丁词根 dominus（主人）建起一个「统治」小词族：dominate、predominant、predominance、predominantly。

latinIntro.en: Latin dominus means lord, and dominari means to be lord or to rule, so every English word in this family keeps the idea of control.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dominus 意为主人，dominari 意为做主人、统治，因此这个词族的英语词都保留了「控制」的含义。

items.example: Dominus is the noble title that gives the root its ruling meaning.
items.exampleCN: dominus 是表示主人的称呼，赋予词根统治意味。

items.example: Dominate is the shortest English word in the family.
items.exampleCN: dominate 是这个词族里最短的英语词。

items.example: In genetics, a dominant trait appears over a recessive one.
items.exampleCN: 在遗传学里，显性性状压过隐性性状。

items.example: The prefix pre- adds the sense of coming first.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pre- 加上「在先」的意思。

items.example: The predominant mood of the meeting was calm.
items.exampleCN: 会议的主要气氛是平静。

items.example: The predominance of cheap housing shapes the district.
items.exampleCN: 廉价住房占多数，塑造了这一地区的面貌。

items.example: The town is predominantly residential.
items.exampleCN: 这个小镇以住宅为主。

items.meaning: a state ruled by a king
items.example: Kingdom keeps the same old root as dominus.
items.exampleCN: kingdom 与 dominus 共用古老的词根。

definition_zh: 预制；预先制造；预先编排
definition_en: to make the parts of a building or product in a factory before they are put together
core_image: 一堵墙在工厂里先做好，再吊到工地插进去
scene: 港口边的工地上，钢梁和楼板都不是现场浇的，而是先在厂房里造好、再一块块吊到海边拼起来。The harbour tower was prefabricated in a factory before it reached open water.
sceneCN: 这里 prefabricate 是「预制、预先在工厂制造」，对应第 1 个义项：在工厂里把部件造好再运到现场；句意：这座港口塔楼在运到海上之前就已经在工厂里预制好了。

collocations.zh: 预制式的讲话；套话连篇的讲话

derivatives.zh: prefabricate 去词尾加名词后缀 -ion，义为「预制、预制工序」
过去分词作形容词，义为「预制的」
prefabricated 的截短形式，义为「预制件；预制房屋」，也可作形容词
去除前缀 pre- 的基础动词，义为「制造；捏造」

senses.title: To make parts away from the site
senses.definition: to make the parts of a building or machine in a factory before they are put together on site
senses.definitionCN: 在工厂里先把建筑或机器的部件造好，再运到现场拼装
senses.example: The floors of this tower were prefabricated in a yard nearby.
senses.exampleCN: 这座塔楼的楼板是在附近的工场里预制的。
senses.why: The prefix pre- means before and fabricari means to make, so prefabricate is literally to make beforehand.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 pre- 表示「预先」，fabricari 表示制造，因此 prefabricate 字面就是「先造出来」。

senses.title: Something made in advance
senses.definition: made earlier in a factory so that it can be assembled quickly
senses.definitionCN: 事先在工厂做好，以便快速组装的
senses.example: Prefabricated walls arrived by lorry each morning.
senses.exampleCN: 每天早晨，预制的墙体用卡车运到。
senses.why: Once the verb exists, the past participle becomes an adjective describing things that were made beforehand.
senses.whyCN: 动词一旦存在，过去分词就变成形容词，描述提前造好的东西。

senses.title: The making of such parts
senses.definition: the process of making building parts in a factory
senses.definitionCN: 在工厂里制作建筑部件的过程
senses.example: Prefabrication cut the building time by half.
senses.exampleCN: 预制建筑把建造时间缩短了一半。
senses.why: The noun -ion ending turns the action into a process that engineers can plan and schedule.
senses.whyCN: 名词后缀 -ion 把动作变成一个工程师可以规划和排期的工序。

senses.title: Ready-made shortcuts
senses.titleCN: 预制构件式的；现成的套路
senses.definition: used for ready-made phrases or solutions that are not tailored to a situation
senses.definitionCN: 形容照搬现成、未经量身设计的说法或方案
senses.example: His speech was full of prefabricated slogans.
senses.exampleCN: 他的讲话里塞满了现成的口号。
senses.why: The factory image transfers to language: a ready-made phrase is assembled from stock parts, not crafted on the spot.
senses.whyCN: 工厂的意象被搬到语言上：现成的说法是用库存零件拼出来的，不是当场打磨的。

senses.title: Staged rather than natural
senses.titleCN: 包装做作的；预先编排的
senses.definition: planned and staged in advance so that it looks less natural
senses.definitionCN: 事先编排布置好，因而显得不自然
senses.example: The success of the press event felt prefabricated.
senses.exampleCN: 那场媒体活动的成功显得像是预先编排好的。
senses.why: If a house arrives in pieces and is simply slotted together, the result can look planned rather than grown, and this image extends to emotions and events.
senses.whyCN: 如果房子是拆成部件再插接起来，结果就会像是规划的而不是自然生长的，这一画面又延伸到情感与事件。

intro.en: Prefabricate joins Latin prae-, before, to fabricare, to make, which comes from faber, a craftsman or smith.
intro.cn: prefabricate 把拉丁语 prae-（在前）与 fabricare（制造）拼在一起，而 fabricare 又来自 faber（工匠、铁匠）。

items.en: Faber means craftsman or smith, and fabrica means a workshop, from which fabricari, to make, develops.
items.cn: 拉丁语 faber 意为工匠、铁匠，fabrica 意为作坊，由此发展出动词 fabricari（制造）。

items.en: The prefix prae-, meaning before, joins fabricare in later Latin to express making beforehand.
items.cn: 前缀 prae-（在前）在后期拉丁语中与 fabricare 结合，表示提前制造。

items.en: Middle English fabric means a building or a structure, while the verb fabricate appears later.
items.cn: 中古英语 fabric 指建筑物或结构，动词 fabricate 出现得更晚。

items.en: Industrial building brings prefabricate into common use for factory-made parts.
items.cn: 工业化建筑让 prefabricate 成为指「工厂预制部件」的常用词。

items.en: The noun prefabrication develops, and prefab becomes everyday short form.
items.cn: 名词 prefabrication 随之形成，prefab 成为日常的缩写形式。

note.en: The prefabric- family sits close to fabricate, and the idea of assembling ready-made parts links the word to assemble and precast.
note.cn: prefabric- 这一族与 fabricate 相邻，而「组装现成部件」的意思又把这个词与 assemble、precast 联系起来。

entries.definition: made in advance in parts
the making of parts in advance
to make, or to invent falsely
to put parts together
formed in a mould before use
ready-made rather than natural

normalIntro.en: Prefabricate is a simple recipe: pre- puts the work before the site, and fabricate supplies the making.
normalIntro.cn: prefabricate 的构成很简单：pre- 把工作放到现场之前，fabricate 提供「制造」。

normal.en: Break it as pre plus fabricate, and remember fabric as woven cloth from the same workshop root.
normal.cn: 拆成 pre 加 fabricate，再记住 fabric（织物）也出自同一个「作坊」词根。

normal.en: A prefabricated house arrives by lorry in panels and is bolted together in a day.
normal.cn: 预制房屋用卡车成片运来，一天内就能用螺栓拼好。

normal.en: The noun prefabrication names the whole factory process, while prefab is the short form.
normal.cn: 名词 prefabrication 指整个工厂工序，prefab 是它的缩写。

normal.en: Compare fabricate: it also means to invent falsely, which explains prefabricated excuses.
normal.cn: 对比 fabricate：它也有「捏造」的意思，这就解释了 prefabricated excuses（编好的借口）。

normal.en: Use prefabricated for anything ready-made rather than made to fit, from walls to speeches.
normal.cn: prefabricated 可形容任何现成而非量身定做的东西，从墙体到讲话。

abstract.en: Think of a jigsaw already cut in the factory, waiting only to be slotted into place.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅在工厂里就已经切好的拼图，只等倒进框里。

abstract.en: Picture a meal frozen at the factory, so dinner takes minutes instead of hours.
abstract.cn: 想象一份在工厂里冻好的饭菜，晚饭只需几分钟而不是几个小时。

abstract.en: Writers often say prefabricated feelings when they mean emotions that are planned rather than real.
abstract.cn: 写作者常用「prefabricated feelings」形容预先设计而非真实的情感。

examples.en: The school was prefabricated in sections and shipped to the island.
examples.cn: 这所学校被分段预制后运到了岛上。

examples.en: Prefabricated homes can be assembled in days.
examples.cn: 预制房屋几天之内就能组装完成。

examples.en: Critics saw the ceremony as a prefabricated display of unity.
examples.cn: 批评者把那场仪式看作预先编排出来的团结展示。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞fabric吃」——普瑞先把布（fabric）预先织好，现场只是缝一缝；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ fabricare（制造，来自 faber「工匠」）→ 英语 prefabricate，核心义「先造好部件、再拼装」。

sensesIntro.en: Prefabricate begins as a building verb, then turns adjective and noun, and finally extends to phrases and feelings made in advance.
sensesIntro.cn: prefabricate 先是建筑动词，再派生出形容词和名词，最后扩展到预先造好的说法与情感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall built in a factory and lifted into place on site.
core.cn: 核心意象：一堵墙在工厂造好，再吊装到现场。

branches.en: The verb is the everyday building sense.
branches.cn: 动词义项是日常的建筑用法。

branches.en: The past participle turns the making into a description of things.
branches.cn: 过去分词把「制造」变为对事物的描述。

branches.en: The noun names the factory process itself.
branches.cn: 名词义项命名的是工厂工序本身。

branches.en: Phrases and emotions that look assembled rather than natural.
branches.cn: 说法与情感都像拼装出来的，而非自然而然。

branches.en: Both the act and the result depend on parts made beforehand.
branches.cn: 动作与结果都依赖于提前造好的部件。

intro.en: The prefabric- family shares a workshop root with fabricate, fabrication, and prefabrication.
intro.cn: prefabric- 词族与 fabricate、fabrication、prefabrication 共用「作坊」词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin faber, a craftsman, gives fabrica, a workshop, and fabricari, to make, so the family is always about skilled making by hand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 faber（工匠）给出 fabrica（作坊）与 fabricari（制造），这个词族始终与手工技艺相关。

items.example: Faber is the craftsman whose work gives the root its shape.
items.exampleCN: faber 是工匠，其劳作赋予词根形态。

items.example: Fabrica names the place where things are made.
items.exampleCN: fabrica 指制造东西的场所。

items.example: Fabricate covers both building and inventing.
items.exampleCN: fabricate 兼顾制造与捏造。

items.meaning: the act of making or inventing
items.example: Fabrication is the noun of the workshop root.
items.exampleCN: fabrication 是这一作坊词根的名词。

items.example: Fabric shows the same root as cloth made by hand.
items.exampleCN: fabric 体现同源词根，指手工织成的布。

items.example: The prefix pre- puts the making ahead of time.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pre- 把制造放到时间之前。

items.example: Prefabrication keeps the workshop image.
items.exampleCN: prefabrication 保留了作坊意象。

items.example: Prefab is the clipped, everyday form.
items.exampleCN: prefab 是日常的缩写形式。

definition_zh: 前缀；称谓；区号；预先加在前
definition_en: a letter group added to the front of a word, or something fixed in front of another thing
core_image: 一个小标签被钉在词头的最前面
scene: 老师在白板上写字头，把它钉在一个词前面，这个词的意思立刻变了，台下的学生都抬头看。One common prefix, un, can turn a calm word into its opposite.
sceneCN: 这里 prefix 是「前缀」，对应第 1 个义项：加在单词开头、改变词义的字母组合；句意：像 un- 这样的前缀可以改变一个词的意思。

derivatives.zh: prefix 加名词后缀 -ation，义为「添加前缀」
过去分词作形容词，义为「带有前缀的」
现在分词作名词，义为「加前缀的过程」
加形容词后缀 -al，义为「前缀的」

senses.title: A form attached to the front
senses.definition: a letter or group of letters added to the beginning of a word to change its meaning
senses.definitionCN: 加在单词开头、用来改变词义的字母或字母组合
senses.example: The prefix un- turns happy into unhappy.
senses.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 把 happy 变成 unhappy。
senses.why: The Latin verb praefigere means to fasten in front, so a prefix is something glued to the front of a word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 praefigere 意为「在前面钉上」，因此前缀就是钉在词头的东西。

senses.title: A title before a name
senses.definition: a word such as Mr, Dr, or Sir placed before a person name
senses.definitionCN: 放在人名之前、如 Mr 或 Dr 或 Sir 这样的称呼词
senses.example: In Britain, Dr is the usual prefix for a doctor.
senses.exampleCN: 在英国，Dr 是医生常用的称谓前缀。
senses.why: A title is attached in front of the name, exactly like a form attached to the start of a word.
senses.whyCN: 称谓是钉在名字前面的东西，与钉在词头的形式一模一样。

senses.title: A number before a code
senses.definition: a number or set of digits that comes before a telephone or reference number
senses.definitionCN: 出现在电话号码或编号之前的数字
senses.example: Dial the prefix first, then the number.
senses.exampleCN: 先拨区号，再拨号码。
senses.why: In numbers the front part is often a dialling code added in front of the main number, so the image gives a third sense.
senses.whyCN: 在数字里，前面那一段常常是拨号前加上的区号，于是同一画面生出第三种含义。

senses.title: The front part of a set
senses.definition: the first part of a name, code, or set of items
senses.definitionCN: 名称、编码或一组项目中最前面的部分
senses.example: Files with the prefix draft are kept apart.
senses.exampleCN: 以 draft 开头的文件被单独存放。
senses.why: The general idea of what comes first gets almost free from the front position, giving a broad label for the initial part.
senses.whyCN: 「在前」的位置本身几乎免费地给出「开头一段」这个泛义，可以指任何一组事物的首部。

senses.title: To set something before
senses.definition: to place a word or item at the front of something else
senses.definitionCN: 把某个词或项目放到别的东西前面
senses.example: Please prefix each answer with a number.
senses.exampleCN: 请在每个答案前面加上编号。
senses.why: The verb keeps the original Latin action of fastening in front, now applied to words and labels.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了拉丁语原义「钉在前面」，只是作用对象变成了词语和标签。

senses.title: Something put in front by law
senses.definition: a formal statement or condition placed at the head of a law or document
senses.definitionCN: 加在法律或文件开头的正式说明或条件
senses.example: The court examined the prefix of the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 法院审查了合同的前置条款。
senses.why: When a document gains a front section fixed by law, the same front position takes on official weight.
senses.whyCN: 当文件加上一个由法律固定的前置部分时，同样的「前面」位置就有了官方分量。

intro.en: Prefix is a Latin compound of prae-, in front, and figere, to fasten, exactly the picture of a label pinned at the head of a word.
intro.cn: prefix 是拉丁语 prae-（在前）与 figere（钉住）的合成词，正是一个标签钉在词头上的画面。

items.en: Figere means to fix or fasten, and the prefix prae- means in front, giving praefigere, to fasten in front.
items.cn: 拉丁语 figere 意为固定、钉住，前缀 prae- 意为在前，合成 praefigere（钉在前面）。

items.en: The noun praefixum means something fixed on in front, and grammarians use it for particles placed before words.
items.cn: 名词 praefixum 指固定在前面的东西，语法学家用它指放在词前的小品词。

items.en: Old French prefixe or préfixe carries the grammatical term into medieval Europe.
items.cn: 古法语 prefixe 或 préfixe 把这个语法术语带入中世纪欧洲。

items.en: English takes prefix as a grammatical term, and the verb follows it.
items.cn: 英语借入 prefix 作为语法术语，动词随后出现。

items.en: The word widens to titles, telephone codes, and the front part of anything, while its own structure stays pre plus fix.
items.cn: 后来词义扩展到称谓、电话区号以及任何东西的开头，而其结构始终是 pre 加 fix。

note.en: Prefix has a close form family in prefixed and prefixation, and it sits at the head of the affix family beside suffix and infix.
note.cn: prefix 有 prefixed、prefixation 这样的形近词族，又处在词缀家族的开头，与 suffix、infix 并列。

entries.definition: having something put in front
the adding of a prefix
relating to a prefix
a form added at the end
a form inserted inside a word
any form added to a root

normalIntro.en: Prefix is a label at the front: pre- says front, and fix says pinned on.
normalIntro.cn: prefix 就是贴在前面的标签：pre- 说「前」，fix 说「钉上」。

normal.en: Un- in unhappy and re- in rewrite are the clearest everyday prefixes.
normal.cn: unhappy 里的 un- 和 rewrite 里的 re- 是最清楚的两个日常前缀。

normal.en: The word is its own example: pre- is a prefix and fix is the root it is attached to.
normal.cn: 这个词本身就是例子：pre- 是前缀，fix 是它挂上的词根。

normal.en: Remember the pair suffix, which sits at the end, so prefix and suffix differ only in front and back.
normal.cn: 记住成对的 suffix（坐在末尾），prefix 与 suffix 只差在前还是在后。

normal.en: On forms and records, the prefix is the short code that comes before the main number.
normal.cn: 在表格和档案里，prefix 是指写在主编号前面的短代码。

normal.en: As a verb, prefix each answer with a letter when a test uses sections.
normal.cn: 作动词时，考试分节就让每个答案前面加一个字母。

abstract.en: Think of a name sticker stuck at the top corner of a notebook.
abstract.cn: 想象一张姓名贴纸贴在笔记本的右上角。

abstract.en: Picture a train station code before the track number on a ticket.
abstract.cn: 想象车票上写在车厢号前面的车站代码。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand hammering a small plate onto the very front of a box.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一块小牌子钉在箱子的最前面。

examples.en: The prefix bi- means two, as in bicycle.
examples.cn: 前缀 bi- 表示「二」，如 bicycle。

examples.en: Please prefix your file name with the date.
examples.cn: 请在你的文件名前面加上日期。

examples.en: The telephone prefix tells which district the line is in.
examples.cn: 电话区号说明这条线路属于哪个地区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞fix」——普瑞（pre）先把东西 fix 在最前面，就是前缀；pre 与 fix 都是真实成分，谐音只是帮记位置。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ figere（固定、钉住）→ praefixum → 英语 prefix，核心义「钉在前面的东西」。

sensesIntro.en: Prefix starts as something pinned to the front of a word, then names titles and codes at the front of names or numbers, and finally serves as a verb and a legal heading.
sensesIntro.cn: prefix 先在单词前面钉上东西，再指名字或号码前面的称谓与区号，最后用作动词和文件前置条款。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small label pinned to the very front of a word.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张小标签钉在单词的最前面。

branches.en: The grammar sense is the main modern use.
branches.cn: 语法义项是现代最主要的用法。

branches.en: Titles are names pinned before a person name.
branches.cn: 称谓就是钉在人名之前的称呼。

branches.en: Codes are digits pinned before a number.
branches.cn: 区号就是钉在号码之前的一串数字。

branches.en: Any front part, including a legal heading, stays in the same position.
branches.cn: 任何前置部分，包括法律条款前面的说明，都处在同一位置。

branches.en: The verb simply performs what the noun names.
branches.cn: 动词只是把名词所指的动作做出来。

intro.en: Prefix is built from pre- and fix, and its own family includes prefixed, prefixation, and prefixal.
intro.cn: prefix 由 pre- 与 fix 构成，它自己的词族包括 prefixed、prefixation、prefixal。

latinIntro.en: Latin figere, to fasten, also gives fix, fixture, and affix, so the family is always about pinning one thing to another.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 figere（固定）还给出 fix、fixture、affix，这一词族始终围绕「把一样东西钉到另一样上」。

items.example: Figere is the fastening act behind the word.
items.exampleCN: figere 是这个词背后的钉住动作。

items.example: The prefix pre- gives the front position.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pre- 给出前面的位置。

items.meaning: a form attached to a word
items.example: Affix is the general name for prefixes and suffixes.
items.exampleCN: affix 是前缀与后缀的通称。

items.example: The root -fix appears in both prefix and suffix.
items.exampleCN: 词根 -fix 同时出现在 prefix 与 suffix 里。

items.meaning: a form added at the end
items.example: Suffix is the mirror position of prefix.
items.exampleCN: suffix 是与前缀对称的位置。

items.example: Fix is the plain English word from the same root.
items.exampleCN: fix 是同一词根来的普通英语词。

items.example: Fixture shows how fixed in place is the basic idea.
items.exampleCN: fixture 体现「固定在位」是基本含义。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms prefixation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 prefixation。

items.meaning: adding a prefix to a word
items.example: Prefixation is the action behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: prefixation 是名词背后的动作。

definition_zh: 怀孕；孕期；（言辞等的）深意；意味深长；充实、孕育期
definition_en: the condition or period of being pregnant, or the quality of holding much meaning inside
core_image: 腹部渐渐鼓起的隆起，里面藏着还没露面的小生命
scene: 产检报告单送到家里，父母看完第一行就笑了。The clinic report reached the house, and the first line confirmed her pregnancy.
sceneCN: 这里 pregnancy 是「怀孕、孕期」（第 1 个义项）；句意：诊所的报告送到家里，第一行证实了她怀孕。

pos.zh: （言辞、事件中的）深意；充实；孕育期

derivatives.zh: 由 pregnancy 去掉名词后缀 -cy 得到的形容词，义为「怀孕的；意味深长的」
pregnant 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「意味深长地」
拉丁前缀 im-（向内、进入）加 pregnant 的词根，义为「使怀孕；浸透」
pregnancy 的常见搭配同现词，前缀 pre-（之前）加 natal（出生的），义为「产前的」

senses.title: The state of carrying a baby before birth
senses.definition: the condition in which a woman or female animal carries a developing young inside the body before giving birth
senses.definitionCN: 女性或雌性动物在分娩前体内孕育着正在发育的幼体的状态
senses.example: Doctors confirm that early care improves the outcome of a pregnancy.
senses.exampleCN: 医生确认，尽早照护能改善怀孕的结果。
senses.why: The Latin adjective praegnans means bearing before birth, so the core image is a body already carrying what has not yet arrived.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praegnans 本义是「产仔之前」，核心意象就是那副怀而未生的身子，因此这个词首先指怀孕的状态。

senses.title: The period during which a baby develops
senses.definition: the length of time from conception to birth, usually counted in weeks or months
senses.definitionCN: 从受孕到分娩所经历的时间长度，通常按周或按月计算
senses.example: Human pregnancy centers near a length of forty weeks from conception.
senses.exampleCN: 人类孕期从受孕算起大致接近四十周。
senses.why: A condition with a stated beginning and end is naturally measured, so the state word also names a span of time.
senses.whyCN: 既然怀孕有起点也有终点，这个状态自然被量化为一段时长，于是 pregnancy 又指「孕期的几个月」。

senses.title: A swollen abdomen shaped like a womb
senses.definition: a large rounded bulge, especially a belly, that suggests the shape of a late-stage pregnancy
senses.definitionCN: 尤指圆鼓鼓的大肚子，形状让人联想到孕晚期，多见于幽默说法
senses.example: He rubbed his beer pregnancy with both hands and laughed.
senses.exampleCN: 他双手摸摸自己喝啤酒喝圆的肚子，笑了起来。
senses.why: The swelling belly is the most visible mark of the condition, so in joking speech the belly itself takes the name.
senses.whyCN: 晚期孕妇的腹部是 pregnancy 最醒目的视觉标志，人们便用一个肚子来代指整个状态，产生戏谑的「孕肚」义。

senses.title: Words heavy with unspoken meaning
senses.definition: the quality in a speech, phrase, or event of being full of importance or hidden meaning
senses.definitionCN: 言语、短语或事件中蕴含重要信息或言外之意的特质
senses.example: Critics note the pregnancy of her final sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家注意到她最后那句话意味深长。
senses.why: Latin writers already used a full belly as a figure for a mind or word carrying more than it shows, and English kept that figure.
senses.whyCN: 肚子鼓起意味着里面装着什么，把这一意象从身体挪到语言上，就等于说一段话「肚里有货」，于是有了「意味深长」。

senses.title: A period rich in what is yet to come
senses.definition: a state of holding much potential that has not yet become visible
senses.definitionCN: 蕴含着尚未显现的丰富可能性的状态，如季风前的土地
senses.example: Writers speak of the pregnancy of a season before rain arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 作家们会说起雨季来临前那个季节的孕育意味。
senses.why: The centre of the image is not the child already born but the thing not yet shown, and that part of it transfers to any waiting period.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象的重点不是「已经生出来的东西」，而是「还没出现却已经在里面」，把这个意思推广出去就成了各种「孕育期」。

intro.en: Pregnancy comes from the Latin adjective praegnans, already bearing, modified by the Latin noun suffix -ia and carried through English -ancy.
intro.cn: pregnancy 来自拉丁语形容词 praegnans（已经怀着的），加上拉丁名词词尾 -ia，经英语的 -ancy 进入现代用法。

items.en: The adjective praegnans means with child, being before birth, and is the direct source of the English word family.
items.cn: 形容词 praegnans 表示「怀着孩子的」「出生之前的」，是这一英语词族的直接来源。

items.en: A common analysis splits it as prae, meaning before, and gn-, from the same root as gignere, to be born.
items.cn: 常见分析把它拆成 prae（在前）与 gn-（与 gignere「生育、产生」同根）。

items.en: Some scholars doubt that internal origin and compare gnavus, active, or the earlier form praegnas, so the exact stem is uncertain.
items.cn: 也有学者怀疑这种内在来源，而把它和 gnavus（勤于……的）或者更早的形式 praegnas 相比，所以确切词干存疑。

items.en: The English adjective pregnant appears in the fourteenth century from Old French, meaning with child.
items.cn: 英语形容词 pregnant 于十四世纪经古法语出现，意思是怀孕的。

items.en: The abstract noun pregnancy is recorded from the sixteenth century, naming the state rather than the person.
items.cn: 抽象名词 pregnancy 见于十六世纪，指称状态而非人。

items.en: Since the sixteenth century the word has also described speech and situations full of hidden meaning.
items.cn: 自十六世纪起，这个词也用来形容蕴含深意的言语和情境。

note.en: Pregnancy belongs to the Latin word family of pregnant and impregnate, and it sits in the medical field shared with gestation, maternity, and fetus.
note.cn: pregnancy 属于 pregnant 与 impregnate 所在的拉丁词族，并与 gestation、maternity、fetus 共享医学语义场。

entries.definition: carrying a developing baby, or full of meaning
to make pregnant or to fill thoroughly with a substance
reigning or dominant, from Latin regnare to rule
entries.definitionCN: 统治的；占支配地位的。只是拼写相近，词源不同：它来自拉丁语 regnare（统治）。

entries.definition: the period during which a fetus develops inside the womb
the state of being a mother or the period around giving birth
an unborn young that is visibly formed in the womb

normalIntro.en: Pregnancy is the noun of pregnant, a Latin word meaning bearing before birth, and it names the state rather than the person.
