normalIntro.cn: pregnancy 是 pregnant 的名词形式，拉丁语原义是「产之前就怀着」，它指状态而不是人。

normal.en: Pregnant means with child, and the suffix -cy turns that condition into a noun, so pregnancy is the whole state.
normal.cn: pregnant 意为怀孕的，名词后缀 -cy 把这一状态变成名词，所以 pregnancy 就是整个怀孕状态。

normal.en: Linguists connect the Latin root with gignere, to give birth, which also hides in generation and congenital.
normal.cn: 语言学家把拉丁词根与 gignere（生育）联系起来，这个词根也藏在 generation 和 congenital 里。

normal.en: A pregnancy test checks for the hormone label hCG, short for human chorionic gonadotropin.
normal.cn: 妊娠检测查的是 hCG 这种激素，它是人绒毛膜促性腺激素的缩写。

normal.en: Prenatal care means care before birth, built from pre- meaning before and natal meaning of birth.
normal.cn: prenatal care（产前保健）由 pre-（之前）与 natal（出生的）构成。

normal.en: The abstract sense of a pregnant pause is native to the Latin image of a filled belly, so a silence can be pregnant with meaning.
normal.cn: 「意味深长的停顿」这一抽象说法来自拉丁语「装满的肚子」的意象，所以沉默也可以 be pregnant with meaning（充满意味）。

abstract.en: Picture a soft round shadow on a wall, growing slowly heavier month after month.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上一个柔和的圆形影子，一个月比一个月更沉、更圆。

abstract.en: Imagine a sealed seed pod swelling in the sun, keeping its contents unseen.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗荚果在阳光下鼓起来，里面的东西一直看不见。

abstract.en: Think of a sentence that stops early and makes everyone lean forward for the rest.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话说到一半就停住，让所有人都探身等待下文。

examples.en: She followed her doctor on a standard routine during the pregnancy.
examples.cn: 怀孕期间，她一直按医生的标准流程做检查。

examples.en: The word carries its own pregnancy in that final comma.
examples.cn: 那个逗号让这个词自有一份深意。

examples.en: Moderate exercise is usually safe at every stage of a normal pregnancy.
examples.cn: 在正常孕期的每个阶段，适度运动通常是安全的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞格南西」——读到「格南西」不妨联想「搁着南边的西瓜」，肚子里搁着一个还没抱出来的小西瓜，这就是怀孕。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 prae（在前）+ gn-（生育，同 gignere「产生」）→ praegnans（怀着孩子的）→ 古法语 pregnant → 英语 pregnancy（怀孕的状态），一般认为词干 gn- 的切分有争议，故只作「常见分析」处理。

sensesIntro.en: Pregnancy starts from the concrete carrying of a baby, spreads to its measured length and its outward shape, then moves to meaning that is held but not yet fully shown.
sensesIntro.cn: pregnancy 从「体内怀着孩子」这一具体状态出发，扩展为可计量的孕期和外在可见的隆起形状，再比喻为「含着、藏着、尚未完全显露」的意味。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rounded belly that holds an unseen life.
core.cn: 核心意象：鼓起的腹部里藏着看不见的小生命。

branches.en: The concrete state of carrying a child anchors the word.
branches.cn: 怀有孩子的具体状态是词义的落脚点。

branches.en: Naming the state also names how long it lasts.
branches.cn: 既然给状态命名，自然也会用它指这段状态持续多久。

branches.en: The belly that would be a baby is the most visible part and becomes playfully renamed a pregnancy.
branches.cn: 本该孕育孩子的肚子是最显眼的部分，玩笑中它本身就被叫作 pregnancy。

branches.en: Holding a life inside becomes a picture of speech holding a second meaning.
branches.cn: 体内孕有生命，被挪用来比喻言语里还藏着一层意思。

branches.en: Both a real womb and a quiet season carry what has not appeared yet.
branches.cn: 真正的子宫和安静的季节一样，都装着尚未出现的东西。

intro.en: Pregnancy is built around the Latin stem prae-gn-, with the abstract noun suffix -ancy marking a state, and it shares relatives with pregnant, impregnate, and generate.
intro.cn: pregnancy 围绕拉丁词干 prae-gn- 构成，抽象名词后缀 -ancy 表示状态，并与 pregnant、impregnate、generate 共享亲属词。

latinIntro.en: In Latin, prae means before and gn-, from gignere, means to be born, while -ia and -antia form abstract nouns.
latinIntro.cn: 在拉丁语中，prae 意为在前，gn- 源自 gignere（生育），而 -ia 与 -antia 构成抽象名词。

items.example: The prefix marks what comes before birth.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出「出生之前」。

items.meaning: to beget, to cause to be born
items.example: The family shares a link with the verb gignere.
items.exampleCN: 这个词族与动词 gignere 有联系。

items.example: The suffix turns an adjective into a state noun.
items.exampleCN: 该后缀把形容词变成状态名词。

items.meaning: carrying a child, full of meaning
items.example: Pregnant is the everyday adjective.
items.exampleCN: pregnant 是日常形容词。

items.example: Pregnancy is the ordinary state noun.
items.exampleCN: pregnancy 是常用的状态名词。

items.example: The suffix -ly builds the adverb pregnantly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成副词 pregnantly。

items.example: Prenatal care comes from Latin natalis, of birth.
items.exampleCN: prenatal care 中的 natal 来自拉丁语 natalis（出生）。

items.example: Impregnate adds the suffix -ate to the same stem.
items.exampleCN: impregnate 在同词干后加 -ate。

items.example: Impregnation names the act of these things.
items.exampleCN: impregnation 表示使怀孕或浸透的行为。

latinEntries.meaning: the earlier form of the same adjective
latinEntries.meaningCN: 同一形容词较早的形式

definition_zh: 史前时期；史前史；（事件真实的）前史、酝酿阶段
definition_en: the time before written records began, or the unrecorded story behind a later event
core_image: 一座刻着文字的界碑，左边是空白的荒原，右边才开始有人写字记录
scene: 博物馆展厅里，玻璃柜前摆着一根磨光的石矛。In the hall a polished stone spear stood before the case, dated by prehistory alone.
sceneCN: 这里 prehistory 是「史前时期」（第 1 个义项）；句意：展厅里一根磨光的石矛立在玻璃柜前，它的年代只能靠史前时期来断定。

pos.zh: 前史；（事件发生前的）酝酿阶段

derivatives.zh: 由 prehistory 把名词后缀 -y 换成形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「史前的；老掉牙的」
prehistoric 加副词后缀 -ally，义为「从史前时期的角度」
prehistory 加表「人」的后缀 -ian，义为「史前研究者」
去掉前缀 pre- 后的历史分支形容词，义为「历史上重要的」

senses.title: The time before written records
senses.definition: the very long period of human activity that ended when people began to keep written records
senses.definitionCN: 人类活动延续的漫长时期，止于人们开始留下书面记录的年代
senses.example: Stone tools are the main evidence we have from prehistory.
senses.exampleCN: 石器是我们了解史前时期的主要证据。
senses.why: The prefix pre- means before and history means the written account of the past, so the word literally covers everything before the record begins.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 pre- 意为「之前」，history 意为「对过去的书面记述」，所以这个词字面上就是书面记录开始之前的一切。

senses.title: The subject that studies that period
senses.definition: the academic subject or scholarly study of the period before written records
senses.definitionCN: 把上述时期作为研究对象的学科或学问
senses.example: Her research lies at the border between archaeology and prehistory.
senses.exampleCN: 她的研究处在考古学与史前史的交叉地带。
senses.why: Like other names of periods such as history, the word can name the discipline taught in a university as well as the time itself.
senses.whyCN: 既然 history 既能指时间也能指学科，仿照它造出的 prehistory 也就同样可以用来指一门课、一个研究方向。

senses.title: Facts known only from remains, not from text
senses.titleCN: 仅凭证物得知的史前状况
senses.definition: beliefs or conditions of an early group known only from physical evidence instead of written accounts
senses.definitionCN: 早期人群的观念、生活方式，只能依靠实物证据而非文字记载推断，多见于宗教与习俗研究
senses.example: Anthropologists debate the prehistory of fire worship.
senses.exampleCN: 人类学家争论火崇拜的史前状况。
senses.why: Because nothing was written down, every claim about the period is an inference from remains, so the word often marks knowledge held about a group before any text describes it.
senses.whyCN: 因为当时没有文字，一切说法都只能从遗物推断，于是这个词常用来标记「在文字出现之前就已经通行、但只能还原出的情况」。

senses.title: The unrecorded run-up to a later event
senses.titleCN: 前史；（事件之前的）酝酿阶段
senses.definition: the early development of an event, idea, or conflict before it became public and was recorded
senses.definitionCN: 某个事件、思想或冲突在被公开记载之前所经历的早期发展
senses.example: The paper traces the prehistory of the current trade dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文梳理了当前贸易争端的前史。
senses.why: The boundary is not a fixed date but the point where the record starts, so by analogy any event also has a prehistory in the quiet years before the first line is written.
senses.whyCN: 分界线并不是固定年代，而是「记录开始的那一刻」，所以同理，任何事件在被写进第一条记载之前的那段年月，也都是它的前史。

intro.en: Prehistory is a modern compound of the Latin prefix prae-, through English pre-, and the Greek-derived noun history.
intro.cn: prehistory 是现代英语的组合词，由拉丁前缀 prae-（经英语 pre-）与源自希腊语的 history 合成。

items.en: The noun historia means inquiry or a searching account of what was learned.
items.cn: 希腊语名词 historia 意为探究、对所知之事的追述。

items.en: Latin takes historia as a written account of events, the ancestor of the English word history.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 historia，指对事件的书面记述，是英语 history 的祖先。

items.en: The prefix prae- means before or in front of, and English shortens it to pre-.
items.cn: 前缀 prae- 意为「在……之前」「在……前面」，英语把它缩短为 pre-。

items.en: The compound prehistory appears in the nineteenth century, as scholars needed a label for human life older than any text.
items.cn: 组合词 prehistory 于十九世纪出现，因为学者需要一个说法来指称比任何文字都更古老的人类生活。

items.en: Its adjective prehistoric follows soon after, first for sites and then for anything laughably old.
items.cn: 其形容词 prehistoric 随后不久出现，起初形容遗址，后来也形容老得离谱的东西。

items.en: In modern usage the word also names the unrecorded run-up to a public event.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词也用来指某个公开事件之前未被记录的准备过程。

note.en: Prehistory shares the history family of historic, historian, and historical, and it meets the period words archaeology, antiquity, and paleolithic in the same field.
note.cn: prehistory 与 historic、historian、historical 同属历史词族，并与 archaeology、antiquity、paleolithic 在同一语义场里相邻。

entries.definition: relating to the time before written records
the written account of past events
a person who studies and writes history
respect and admiration that comes from success
entries.definitionCN: 声望；威望。只是拼写相近，词源不同：它来自拉丁语 praestigium（幻术）。

entries.definition: the study of the past through the remains people left behind
ancient times, especially those early enough to be partly recorded
of the earliest part of the Stone Age

normalIntro.en: Prehistory is assembled from English pieces: pre- for before, plus history for the written record.
normalIntro.cn: prehistory 由英语零件拼成：pre- 表示之前，history 表示书面记录。

normal.en: Look at prehistory as two parts in word order: the prefix comes first, the record comes second.
normal.cn: 看 prehistory 的语序：先是前缀，后是记录，前面没人写，后面才开始写。

normal.en: Compare history and story, which both descend from Latin historia, a written account.
normal.cn: 对比 history 与 story，二者都来自拉丁语 historia（书面记述）。

normal.en: The word prehistoric is the everyday adjective, as in prehistoric cave paintings.
normal.cn: prehistoric 是日常形容词，如 prehistoric cave paintings（史前洞窟壁画）。

normal.en: A person who works on the field is called a prehistorian, built with the suffix -ian.
normal.cn: 研究这一领域的人叫 prehistorian，由后缀 -ian 构成。

normal.en: For contrast, protohistory does have some written sources, though outsiders wrote them.
normal.cn: 作为对照，protohistory（原史）其实有少量文字资料，只不过由外人记载。

abstract.en: Picture a stone monument whose carved letters begin only half way across its face.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石碑，刻字只从碑面的一半开始。

abstract.en: Imagine a film reel that starts in darkness and only later shows a picture.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘胶片开头一片漆黑，很久之后才出现画面。

abstract.en: Think of a bonfire whose ashes tell the whole story because nobody was watching.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆篝火，没有人围观，只能靠灰烬来讲述全部经过。

examples.en: The chapter opens with a survey of prehistory in northern Europe.
examples.cn: 这一章以对北欧史前时期的概述开篇。

examples.en: Without writing, prehistory can be reconstructed only from bones and tools.
examples.cn: 缺少文字，史前时期只能靠骨骼和工具来重建。

examples.en: Historians now study the prehistory of the internet itself.
examples.cn: 如今历史学家也在研究互联网自身的前史。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞历史」——「普」通人都还没开始写「历史」，那整个时代自然就叫作 prehistory。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 historia（探究、记述）→ 拉丁语 historia（书面记述）→ 英语 history；再加拉丁前缀 prae-（之前，英语作 pre-），于十九世纪合成 prehistory，核心义「有文字记录之前」。

sensesIntro.en: Prehistory starts as a label for the long age before writing, becomes a subject of study, stands for knowledge known only from remains, and finally stretches to the hidden run-up of any event.
sensesIntro.cn: prehistory 起初是「文字出现前的漫长年代」这一标签，后指一门学科，也指只能靠遗物得知的状况，最后推广到任何事件公开之前那段未被记录的准备期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a marker stone where the blank past meets the first written line.
core.cn: 核心意象：界碑一侧是空白的过去，另一侧才出现第一行字。

branches.en: The era before records is the plain meaning of the word.
branches.cn: 记录出现之前的时代是这个词的本义。

branches.en: A labelled era easily becomes a subject taught in universities.
branches.cn: 一个有名称的时代，很容易进一步成为一门在大学里讲授的学科。

branches.en: With no text to read, all knowledge of the period must be inferred from objects.
branches.cn: 没有文字可读，关于那个时期的一切知识都只能从实物推断。

branches.en: Any event also has quiet years before its first record, so the label moves into ordinary writing.
branches.cn: 任何事件在第一条记录之前也有安静的若干年，所以这个名称被借用到普通写作中。

branches.en: The long blank age and the claims made about it rest on the same absence of text.
branches.cn: 漫长的空白年代与关于它的种种说法，都建立在同一个「没有文字」之上。

intro.en: Prehistory joins the Latin prefix prae-, shortened to pre-, with history, and the family grows through -ic, -ian, and -ally.
intro.cn: prehistory 由拉丁前缀 prae-（缩短为 pre-）与 history 组合而成，词族再通过 -ic、-ian、-ally 等后缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin prae- means before, and historia is a written account, both borrowed into English in smaller pieces.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prae- 意为之前，historia 意为书面记述，两者都分块被英语借用。

items.example: The prefix places the era before the record.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把时代放在记录之前。

items.example: Historia is the ancestor of history.
items.exampleCN: historia 是 history 的祖先。

items.example: History supplies the second half of the word.
items.exampleCN: history 提供这个词的后半部分。

items.example: Prehistory is the compound itself.
items.exampleCN: prehistory 就是这一组合词本身。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms prehistoric.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 构成 prehistoric。

items.example: The suffix -ian forms prehistorian.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ian 构成 prehistorian。

items.example: The suffix -ally forms prehistorically.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ally 构成 prehistorically。

items.example: The prefix builds the contrast term protohistory.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀构成对照词 protohistory。

items.example: The suffix appears in archaeology, the sibling field.
items.exampleCN: 该后缀出现在相邻学科 archaeology 中。

latinEntries.meaning: of history, the form behind the adjective
latinEntries.meaningCN: 历史的，是形容词所依据的形式

definition_zh: 前奏；序曲；序幕；（事件的）前兆
definition_en: a short piece of music or an event that comes before a longer or more important one
core_image: 乐手在正式演奏前先轻轻拨响几个音，为后面的曲子试音
scene: 剧场灯光还没亮，台下已经有人侧耳倾听。The orchestra warmed up with a short prelude before the curtain rose.
sceneCN: 这里 prelude 是「前奏、序曲」（第 1 个义项）；句意：幕布升起前，乐队先用一段短小的前奏试音热身。

pos.zh: 作为前奏；以……为前奏（多与 to 连用）

collocations.zh: 一首 E 小调前奏曲

derivatives.zh: prelude 加形容词后缀 -ial（去掉词尾 e），义为「前奏的；序曲的」
prelude 的词干加名词后缀 -ion，义为「前奏；预示」
prelusion 加形容词后缀 -ive，义为「序幕性的；预兆的」
同源替换：前缀 inter-（之间）加同样的 lud-（玩耍、演奏），义为「间奏；插曲」

senses.title: A short opening piece of music
senses.definition: a short piece of music played before a longer work, such as a fugue, suite, or opera
senses.definitionCN: 在较长乐曲（如赋格、组曲、歌剧）之前演奏的短曲
senses.example: Each prelude on the programme leads into a fugue.
senses.exampleCN: 曲目单上的每一首前奏曲都紧随一首赋格。
senses.why: Latin ludere means to play, and pre- means before, so a prelude is playing that comes first, originally music used to warm up or tune in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ludere 意为演奏，pre- 意为在前，所以前奏就是先响起来的演奏，原指正式唱歌或演奏前的试音。

senses.title: The instrumental opening of an opera
senses.definition: an instrumental passage played before the first act of an opera or other stage work
senses.definitionCN: 歌剧或其他舞台作品第一幕开始前演奏的器乐段落
senses.example: The opera begins with a solemn prelude for strings.
senses.exampleCN: 这部歌剧以一段庄重的弦乐序曲开场。
senses.why: From warm-up playing the word moves to a written opening movement, since staged works needed a tune that gathered the audience before the action.
senses.whyCN: 从临时试音扩展到写定的开头乐章，因为舞台作品需要一个旋律先把观众聚拢到情节之前。

senses.title: Any act that comes before the main one
senses.definition: something that acts as an introduction or first step before the main part
senses.definitionCN: 作为引言或开头第一步、位于主体之前的事物
senses.example: A short speech served as prelude to the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 开幕前的一段简短讲话充当了仪式的序幕。
senses.why: Once the word covers anything played first, it easily covers anything done first, so a speech or ceremony may be called a prelude.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词能指「任何先响起的东西」，也就能指「任何先做的事」，于是讲话、仪式都可以被称为序幕。

senses.title: A warning sign of something bigger
senses.titleCN: 前兆；战争或灾难的先声
senses.definition: a minor event that comes before and hints at something larger or more serious
senses.definitionCN: 在更大或更严重的事之前发生、并为其预热的小事件
senses.example: Fresh raids were a prelude to a full invasion.
senses.exampleCN: 几起新的袭击是一场全面入侵的前兆。
senses.why: If the opening tune is a small version of the whole work, a small event can be cast as a lower-power version of the great event that follows.
senses.whyCN: 既然开头的小曲是整部作品的缩影，那么一个小事件也可以被看作随后大事的低配版本，从而成为「前兆」。

senses.title: To act as a prelude
senses.definition: to come before something as its introduction, used as a verb
senses.definitionCN: 作为某一事物的前奏出现，用作动词
senses.example: Their argument preluded a very long silence.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的争吵成了一段漫长沉默的前奏。
senses.why: English often lets a noun take verb shape where the action is clear, and musical writers already spoke of preluding, so the noun now acts as a verb.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让名词分担动作，音乐写法里早就有 preluding 这样的用法，于是名词也当动词用，表示「作为前奏」。

intro.en: Prelude comes from Latin and Old French words that join pre-, meaning before, with ludere, meaning to play.
intro.cn: prelude 来自拉丁语与古法语，由表示「之前」的 pre- 与表示「演奏、玩耍」的 ludere 组合而成。

items.en: The verb praeludere means to play beforehand, from prae- in front and ludere to play, and is recorded in the late empire.
items.cn: 动词 praeludere 意为「预先演奏」，由 prae-（在前）与 ludere（演奏、玩耍）构成，见于帝国晚期。

items.en: In medieval music praeludium names a short instrumental warm-up before singing or dancing begins.
items.cn: 中世纪音乐术语 praeludium 指演唱或舞蹈开始前短小的器乐试奏。

items.en: The form prelude passes into French, keeping the musical sense of a piece played first.
items.cn: prelude 这一形式进入法语，保持「先演奏的曲子」这一音乐含义。

items.en: Renaissance English borrows prelude for instrumental pieces played before songs, dances, and church music.
items.cn: 文艺复兴时期的英语借入 prelude，指歌曲、舞曲与教堂音乐之前的器乐段。

items.en: Baroque composers such as Johann Sebastian Bach fix the term for independent keyboard pieces that open a larger work.
items.cn: 约翰·塞巴斯蒂安·巴赫等巴洛克作曲家把这一名称固定为开启更大作品的独立键盘曲。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the word also describes any event or act that comes before something greater.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，这个词也用来形容在更大事件之前出现的任何事件或行为。

note.en: Prelude belongs to the ludere family that also gives interlude, collude, and illusion, and in meaning it sits beside overture, prologue, and harbinger.
note.cn: prelude 属于 ludere 词族，同一词族还有 interlude、collude、illusion，在语义上则与 overture、prologue、harbinger 相邻。

entries.definition: a short piece played between the parts of a longer work
to work secretly with another person to do something wrong
a false belief or a trick of the senses
to prevent something from happening
entries.definitionCN: 阻止；排除。只是拼写相近，词源不同：它的词干是拉丁语 claudere（关闭）。

entries.definition: the orchestral music played at the start of an opera
an introduction at the beginning of a play or story
a sign that something is coming

normalIntro.en: Prelude is slotted together from Latin pieces, pre- for before and ludere for playing, so it is playing that comes first.
normalIntro.cn: prelude 由拉丁零件拼成：pre- 表示之前，ludere 表示演奏，合起来就是「先响起的那一段」。

normal.en: The same stem ludere gives interlude, which plays between, and prelude, which plays before.
normal.cn: 同一词干 ludere 既造出中间插入的 interlude，也造出在前演奏的 prelude。

normal.en: In music, a prelude most often opens a set of fugues, suites, or an opera.
normal.cn: 音乐中，前奏曲最常放在一组赋格、组曲或一部歌剧的开头。

normal.en: The adjective form is preludial, as in a preludial chord, built with the suffix -ial.
normal.cn: 形容词形式是 preludial，如 a preludial chord（前奏性和弦），由后缀 -ial 构成。

normal.en: As a verb the word is rare and takes to, as in incidents that prelude to a conflict.
normal.cn: 作动词时这个词较少见，常与 to 连用，如「为冲突作前奏的事件」。

normal.en: Compare overture, which is the fuller orchestral opening for an opera, while a prelude may be shorter and more independent.
normal.cn: 对比 overture（歌剧的完整管弦乐序曲），prelude 往往更短、更独立。

abstract.en: Picture fingers testing a piano keyboard before a hall falls silent.
abstract.cn: 想象在音乐厅安静下来之前，有人先用手指试了试琴键。

abstract.en: Imagine a single doorbell rung long before a whole orchestra arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象整支乐队还没到，门铃先响了一声。

abstract.en: Think of the first drop of rain that tells you the storm is on its way.
abstract.cn: 想象第一滴雨落下，告诉你暴风雨正朝这边赶来。

examples.en: The pianist played a gentle prelude before the sonata began.
examples.cn: 钢琴家在奏鸣曲开始前弹了一段轻柔的前奏曲。

examples.en: Rising food prices were a prelude to the crisis.
examples.cn: 食品价格上涨是这场危机的前兆。

examples.en: A few small preludes for beginners open the album.
examples.cn: 专辑以几首写给初学者的短前奏曲开篇。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞路德」——「路」还没正式走，「德」先跟上了；先热热闹闹来上一小段，正戏才开场。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 prae（在前）+ ludere（演奏、玩耍）→ praeludere（预先演奏）→ 中世纪拉丁语 praeludium（演奏前的短曲）→ 古法语 prelude → 英语 prelude，核心义「先响的、先做的那一段」。

sensesIntro.en: Prelude begins as music played before a song, grows into a fixed opening movement for opera and keyboards, then spreads to any act or event that comes before something greater.
sensesIntro.cn: prelude 起初指唱歌之前先演奏的音乐，成长为歌剧和键盘曲的固定开场乐章，再扩展到任何先于大事发生的行为或事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fingers testing the keys before the real piece begins.
core.cn: 核心意象：正式曲目开始前，手指先试了试琴键。

branches.en: A short piece played first is the musical anchor.
branches.cn: 先演奏的短曲是这个词的音乐根基。

branches.en: Stage works formalised the opening into an orchestra piece.
branches.cn: 舞台作品把这种开场固定成一段管弦乐。

branches.en: Anything done first borrows the name from anything played first.
branches.cn: 任何「先做的」都可以借「先演奏的」这个名号。

branches.en: A small opening figure points forward to the large event behind it.
branches.cn: 开头的小段子指向身后那个大事件，于是一小事件成了前兆。

branches.en: Musical writers already used preluding, so the noun turned into a verb with to.
branches.cn: 音乐写法里早已有 preluding，名词由此转为与 to 连用的动词。

intro.en: Prelude joins the Latin prefix prae-, shortened to pre-, with the Latin root lud, and forms relatives such as interlude, collude, and illusion.
intro.cn: prelude 由拉丁前缀 prae-（缩短为 pre-）与拉丁词根 lud 合成，并衍生出 interlude、collude、illusion 等亲属词。

latinIntro.en: In Latin, prae- means before and ludere means to play, and the -ium ending names the result in praeludium.
latinIntro.cn: 在拉丁语中，prae- 意为之前，ludere 意为演奏，praeludium 的 -ium 词尾表示结果。

items.example: The prefix places the playing first.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把演奏放在前面。

items.example: The root carries the idea of playing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「演奏」的意思。

items.example: Praeludere is the source verb.
items.exampleCN: praeludere 是来源动词。

items.example: Praeludium names the shorter piece.
items.exampleCN: praeludium 指那段先奏的短曲。

items.example: Prelude keeps the musical core.
items.exampleCN: prelude 保留了音乐核心义。

items.example: The prefix builds the sibling word interlude.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀构成兄弟词 interlude。

items.example: The suffix -ial builds preludial.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ial 构成 preludial。

items.example: The suffix -ion builds prelusion.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 构成 prelusion。

items.example: The suffix -ive builds prelusive.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成 prelusive。

definition_zh: 首要的；最重要的；（英国、加拿大等的）首相；总理
definition_en: best or most important of its kind, or the leader of a government in some countries
core_image: 宴席首位上的那个人：全场目光先落在他身上
scene: 晚宴刚开席，大家纷纷举杯，目光都投向主桌最尊贵的那位客人。The hotel is the city premier venue for international conferences.
sceneCN: 这里 premier 是「首要的、首屈一指的」（第 1 个义项：同类中最好或最重要的）；句意：这家酒店是本城举办国际会议的首选场地。

pos.zh: 形容词：首要的；最好的；最先进的
名词：首相；总理；（加拿大）省长

derivatives.zh: 由 premier 加复数后缀构成，义为「多位首相、总理」
由 premier 加 -ship（职位、任期）构成，义为「首相或总理的职位与任期」
由法语首演义借入，与本词同源但已分化，义为「首映；首演」
与 premier 同源于拉丁语 primus（第一），义为「保费；溢价；额外费用」

senses.title: First in rank among similar things
senses.definition: best, most important, or most advanced among things of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 在同类事物中最好、最重要或最先进的
senses.example: She trained at one of Europe top art schools.
senses.exampleCN: 她曾在欧洲一所顶尖的艺术院校受训。
senses.why: The word descends from Latin primus, first, so its first sense is simply being first in rank.
senses.whyCN: 本词来自拉丁语 primus（第一），所以最直接的义项就是「排在第一位」。

senses.title: A leading government office
senses.definition: the head of a government in certain countries, such as Britain or Canada
senses.definitionCN: 英国、加拿大等国的政府首脑
senses.example: The premier announced a new plan for public health.
senses.exampleCN: 总理宣布了一项公共卫生新计划。
senses.why: The person who is first in the government was naturally called the premier.
senses.whyCN: 政府中排在第一位的人，自然就被称作 premier。

senses.title: A head of a province in Canada
senses.definition: the head of a provincial government in Canada
senses.definitionCN: 加拿大各省政府的首脑
senses.example: The provincial premier met the federal minister.
senses.exampleCN: 该省省长会见了联邦部长。
senses.why: The same first-in-rank image transferred to provincial leaders in Canada.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「居首」意象延伸到加拿大省级政府首脑身上。

senses.title: The earliest form on record
senses.definition: used in formal writing for the earliest example or version of something
senses.definitionCN: 正式书面语中表示某事物最早的例子或版本
senses.example: This is the premier example of Roman stone carving.
senses.exampleCN: 这是罗马石雕最早的范例。
senses.why: If something ranks first, it can also be first in time, an older formal use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 既然排在第一位，也就可以指时间上最早，这是较古老的正式用法。

senses.title: A top-level term before a noun
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe the level of a prime minister or the very top level
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，描写总理级别或顶尖水平
senses.example: The two countries held premier-level talks on trade.
senses.exampleCN: 报告呼吁两国举行总理级会谈。
senses.why: The noun sense of a leader grew into an adjective describing that high level.
senses.whyCN: 由指「领导人」的名词义长出，用来形容那种最高层级。

intro.en: Premier comes from French premier, first, from Latin primarius, first in rank, built on primus, first.
intro.cn: premier 来自法语 premier（第一），源于拉丁语 primarius（居首的），底层是 primus（第一）。

items.en: Primus means first in order or rank.
items.cn: primus 意为次序或等级上的第一。

items.en: Primarius means of the first rank.
items.cn: primarius 意为属于第一等级的。

items.en: Premier is formed in French with the meaning first.
items.cn: 法语中形成 premier，意为第一。

items.en: Premier enters English as an adjective meaning first.
items.cn: premier 以形容词身份进入英语，意为第一的。

items.en: The noun comes to name the chief minister of a state.
items.cn: 名词义开始指一国的首席大臣。

items.en: Modern use spreads to sports, media, and provincial leaders.
items.cn: 现代用法扩展到体育、媒体与省级领导人。

note.en: Premier sits beside its Latin relatives primary, prime, and the near synonyms chief and leading.
note.cn: premier 与拉丁同族的 primary、prime 相邻，也与 chief、leading 这类近义词相邻。

entries.definition: first in order or importance
entries.definitionCN: 首要的；基本的（同源于 primus）

entries.definition: first in importance or of the best quality
entries.definitionCN: 首要的；最好的（同源于 primus）

entries.definition: a member of the highest order of mammals
entries.definitionCN: 灵长类动物或首席主教（同源于 primus）

entries.definition: most important or in the highest position
most important or successful
entries.definitionCN: 领先的；最重要或最成功的

entries.definition: the first public performance of a film or play
entries.definitionCN: 首映；首演（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: Premier keeps the Latin image of first place: the front seat, the top league, the head of a government.
normalIntro.cn: premier 保留了拉丁语「第一位」的意象：最前面的座位、最高级别的联赛、政府的首脑。

normal.en: Premier League names the top football league in England.
normal.cn: Premier League 是英格兰足球的最高级别联赛。

normal.en: A premier venue is the best place for an event.
normal.cn: a premier venue 指举办活动最好的场地。

normal.en: Premier and prime share Latin primus, first, with primary.
normal.cn: premier、prime、primary 共享拉丁语 primus（第一）。

normal.en: Premier is the title of the British and Canadian head of government.
normal.cn: premier 是英国与加拿大政府首脑的称谓。

normal.en: Compare premiere: the shorter premier means first or leading, the longer premiere means a first performance.
normal.cn: 对比 premiere：短的 premier 表示首要或顶级，长的 premiere 表示首映或首演。

abstract.en: Picture the guest of honour sitting at the head of the table.
abstract.cn: 想象主宾坐在长桌最顶端的位置。

abstract.en: Imagine a trophy marked with the number one on a podium.
abstract.cn: 想象领奖台上第一名的奖杯。

abstract.en: Think of a photograph already hung in the oldest frame on the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上最旧相框里挂的那张照片，它就是最早的记录。

examples.en: The country premier will visit the flood-hit region tomorrow.
examples.cn: 该国总理明天将视察受灾地区。

examples.en: This laboratory is a premier centre for marine research.
examples.cn: 这个实验室是海洋研究的顶尖中心。

examples.en: Several premier European museums joined the exchange programme.
examples.cn: 几家欧洲顶级博物馆加入了交流计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞米尔」——请想象首相站在最前排，口号里就带着「米」位，第一位就是 premier；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 primus（第一）→ primarius（居首的）→ 法语 premier（第一）→ 英语 premier，核心义「居首、首位」。

sensesIntro.en: Premier starts as an adjective for the first in rank, then names a national leader, a provincial leader, and finally the earliest example.
sensesIntro.cn: premier 最初是形容词，表示排在第一位；随后用来指国家领导人、省长，最后也可指最早出现的例子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the honoured guest at the head of the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：主桌首位上的贵客。

branches.en: The adjective sense names whatever stands first in quality.
branches.cn: 形容词义指在品质上居首的事物。

branches.en: The noun sense names the head of a national government.
branches.cn: 名词义指国家政府首脑。

branches.en: In Canada the noun shifts to a provincial leader.
branches.cn: 在加拿大，名词义转向省级领导人。

branches.en: The earliest example is first in time rather than rank.
branches.cn: 最早的例子指时间上的第一，而不是等级上的第一。

branches.en: The adjective can describe a top level such as a premier conference.
branches.cn: 形容词也可描述顶级层次，如总理级会议。

intro.en: Premier is a borrowed adjective built on the Latin root prim, first, and it shares a family with prime, primary, and primate.
intro.cn: premier 是借入的形容词，建立在拉丁词根 prim（第一）之上，与 prime、primary、primate 同族。

latinIntro.en: Latin primus means first; primarius means of the first rank; the comparative primor is unknown in common use but related forms survive in prince and principal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 primus 意为第一，primarius 意为居首的；相关形式还留在 prince 与 principal 之中。

items.example: The root prim- appears in premier and prime.
items.exampleCN: 词根 prim- 出现在 premier 与 prime 中。

items.example: Premier keeps the adjective sense.
items.exampleCN: premier 保留了形容词义。

items.example: Prime carries the same idea of top quality.
items.exampleCN: prime 带有同样的顶级品质之意。

items.example: Primary adds the adjective suffix -ary.
items.exampleCN: primary 加上形容词后缀 -ary。

items.example: Primate shares the first-in-rank idea.
items.exampleCN: primate 共享「居首」的理念。

items.example: The suffix -ary forms primary and ordinary.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ary 构成 primary 与 ordinary。

items.meaningCN: 表示职位或状态的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ship forms premiership.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ship 构成 premiership。

items.example: The final -re marks a borrowed French spelling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -re 是借自法语拼写的标记。

items.example: Principle shares the first-in-order root.
items.exampleCN: principle 共享「居首」词根。

definition_zh: 首映；首演；首映式；首次播出；首次上演
definition_en: the first public performance or showing of a film, play, or television programme
core_image: 剧场红幕第一次拉开，观众屏息等待
scene: 剧院门口铺着红毯，明星们陆续入场，记者们举着相机等待。The film premiere drew a large crowd to the theatre entrance.
sceneCN: 这里 premiere 是「首映礼」（第 1 个义项：影片首次公开放映的仪式）；句意：影片首映礼在剧院入口吸引了大批人群。

derivatives.zh: 由同一法语词形分化而来，义为「首要的；首相」
由前缀 re-（再次）加本词构成，义为「再映；重演」

senses.title: The first public showing of a film or play
senses.definition: the first public performance or showing of a film, play, or television programme
senses.definitionCN: 影片、戏剧或电视节目首次公开演出或放映
senses.example: The movie had its premiere in London last night.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片昨晚在伦敦首映。
senses.why: French premier, first, picks up the first-in-time image: the very first time a work faces an audience.
senses.whyCN: 法语 premier（第一）给出「第一次」的形象：作品第一次面对观众。

senses.title: The ceremony of a first showing
senses.definition: the formal event or gathering at which the first showing takes place
senses.definitionCN: 举行首次放映或演出的正式活动或聚会
senses.example: Stars walked the red carpet at the premiere.
senses.exampleCN: 明星们在首映礼上走过红毯。
senses.why: The first showing became a social event, so the word also names the ceremony itself.
senses.whyCN: 首次放映变成了社交盛事，因此该词也指首映仪式本身。

senses.title: To show or perform for the first time
senses.definition: to give the first performance or showing of a work
senses.definitionCN: 首次演出或放映某部作品
senses.example: The play premiered in Paris in the last century.
senses.exampleCN: 这部剧上个世纪在巴黎首演。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: to premiere is simply to hold the first performance.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词：to premiere 就是举行首演。

senses.title: A first appearance on television or online
senses.titleCN: 电视或网络的首次播出
senses.definition: the first broadcast of a programme or season
senses.definitionCN: 节目或新一季内容首次播出
senses.example: The quiz show returns with its season premiere tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 这档新闻节目今晚以新一季首播回归。
senses.why: The first-showing image spread from theatres to broadcast schedules.
senses.whyCN: 「首次放映」的意象从剧院扩展到播出时段表。

senses.title: A public debut of a product or fashion
senses.definition: the first public presentation of a design or product
senses.definitionCN: 设计或产品首次公开展示
senses.example: The fashion house held the premiere of its new line.
senses.exampleCN: 这家时装屋举办了新系列的首次亮相。
senses.why: The same first-in-public idea now covers design launches.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「首次公开」概念如今涵盖设计发布。

intro.en: Premiere is the feminine form of French premier, first, from Latin primarius, meaning of the first rank.
intro.cn: premiere 是法语 premier（第一）的阴性形式，源于拉丁语 primarius（居首的）。

items.en: Primus means first in order.
items.cn: primus 意为次序上的第一。

items.en: Premier, with feminine premiere, is formed in French.
items.cn: 法语形成 premier，其阴性形式为 premiere。

items.en: Premiere names the first performance of a play.
items.cn: premiere 开始指戏剧的首场演出。

items.en: English borrows premiere for the first night of a play.
items.cn: 英语借入 premiere，指戏剧的首演之夜。

items.en: Film, then television, add their own premieres.
items.cn: 电影随后是电视，各有各的首映与首播。

items.en: Premiere now also works as a verb.
items.cn: 如今 premiere 也可作动词使用。

note.en: Premiere looks like premier but means a first showing, and it is close to debut and opening.
note.cn: premiere 形似 premier，但意思是首映或首演，与 debut、opening 义近。

entries.definition: first in rank, or a prime minister
entries.definitionCN: 首要的；首相（同源但词义不同）

entries.definition: first in order or importance
entries.definitionCN: 首要的；基本的（同源于 primus）

entries.definition: first in importance
entries.definitionCN: 首要的；最佳的（同源于 primus）

entries.definition: a first public appearance
the first part or first performance of a show
a public event for showing something new

normalIntro.en: Premiere is the feminine of premier, first, so the word is literally the first time.
normalIntro.cn: premiere 是 premier（第一）的阴性形式，所以这个词字面上就是「第一次」。

normal.en: A film premiere is the first public showing of a film.
normal.cn: a film premiere 是影片第一次公开放映。

normal.en: Premiere night is the evening of a first performance.
normal.cn: premiere night 指首演之夜。

normal.en: Premiere and premier share the Latin root prim, first.
normal.cn: premiere 与 premier 共享拉丁词根 prim（第一）。

normal.en: The verb form is premiered, as in the play premiered in spring.
normal.cn: 动词形式是 premiered，如 the play premiered in spring。

normal.en: Compare premiere and premier: one extra letter e marks the first performance.
normal.cn: 对比 premiere 与 premier：多出的字母 e 标记「首演」。

abstract.en: See the red velvet curtain rising for the very first time.
abstract.cn: 想象红色天鹅绒大幕第一次升起。

abstract.en: Picture a row of photographers aiming cameras at the entrance.
abstract.cn: 想象一排摄影师把相机对准剧院入口。

abstract.en: Imagine the first frame of a new season flashing on screen.
abstract.cn: 想象新一季节目的第一帧画面在屏幕上闪出。

examples.en: The opera premiere was sold out weeks in advance.
examples.cn: 这部歌剧的首演几周前就售罄了。

examples.en: Her new series will premiere online next month.
examples.cn: 她的新剧下个月将在网上首播。

examples.en: Guests arrived early for the world premiere of the film.
examples.cn: 嘉宾们提前抵达参加影片的全球首映。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞麦尔——首映」：想象红毯上麦克风林立，大家都叫「米」来抢第一张照片，premiere 就是第一次开演；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 primus（第一）→ primarius（居首的）→ 法语 premier 及阴性 première（第一的）→ 英语 premiere，核心义「第一次公演」。

sensesIntro.en: Premiere begins with the first public showing, then the social ceremony around it, then the verb to première, and finally first broadcasts and product launches.
sensesIntro.cn: premiere 先指首次公开放映，再指围绕它的社交仪式，然后转为动词「首次上演」，最后用于首次播出与新品亮相。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the curtain going up for the first time.
core.cn: 核心意象：大幕第一次升起。

branches.en: The first showing of a film or play is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 影片或戏剧的首次放映是基本义。

branches.en: The party around that showing is the social sense.
branches.cn: 围绕首映的聚会是社交义。

branches.en: The verb sense means to stage that first performance.
branches.cn: 动词义表示举办那场首演。

branches.en: Television keeps the sense for first broadcasts.
branches.cn: 电视沿用该词表示首次播出。

branches.en: A design premiere echoes a film premiere in its public debut.
branches.cn: 汽车首秀与电影首映一样都是首次公开亮相。

intro.en: Premiere is a French borrowing built on the Latin root prim, first, and keeps its French final -re spelling.
intro.cn: premiere 是借自法语的词，建立在拉丁词根 prim（第一）之上，并保留了法语词尾 -re 的拼写。

latinIntro.en: Latin primus means first and primarius means of the first rank; French premier uses that base for the first in rank.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 primus 意为第一，primarius 意为居首的；法语 premier 用这个词基表示居首。

items.example: The root prim- carries the first idea.
items.exampleCN: 词根 prim- 承载「第一」的概念。

items.example: Premiere names a first performance.
items.exampleCN: premiere 指首场演出。

items.example: Premier drops the feminine final e.
items.exampleCN: premier 去掉阴性的词尾 e。

items.example: The suffix -re marks the feminine form.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -re 标记阴性形式。

items.example: The prefix re- means again.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 表示再次。

items.meaning: to show for the first time
items.example: Premiere also works as a verb.
items.exampleCN: premiere 也可作动词。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms premiered.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 premiered。

items.example: Prime shares the same first sense.
items.exampleCN: prime 共享同样的「第一」义。

definition_zh: 全神贯注；满腹心事；关注的焦点；当务之急
definition_en: the state of being so focused on something that you are not aware of other things, or the thing you think about most
core_image: 一个人低头盯着手中的东西，把周围全部挡住
scene: 他在会议中一言不发，手里反复转动着一支笔，眼神停在桌面。His preoccupation with the deadline kept him silent all afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 preoccupation 是「满腹心事、全神贯注」（第 2 个义项：心神被某事占满的状态）；句意：他一心想着截止日期，整个下午都没有说话。

pos.zh: 名词：全神贯注；满腹心事；关注的焦点；当务之急

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「使全神贯注；使担忧」
由动词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「心不在焉的；有心事的」
由动词加现在分词后缀构成，义为「令人牵挂的」
与本词共享拉丁语词根 occupare，义为「职业；占据」

senses.title: The act of capturing attention in advance
senses.definition: the act of taking hold of something in advance
senses.definitionCN: 事先占住或控制某物
senses.example: Military preoccupation of the port came before the talks.
senses.exampleCN: 在谈判之前，港口就已经被军事占领。
senses.why: Latin pre- means before and occupatio means a seizing, so the word first meant a taking hold in advance.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 pre- 表示「预先」，occupatio 表示「占有」，所以本义是「事先占住」。

senses.title: The state of having your mind fully taken
senses.definition: the state of thinking about something so much that you do not notice other things
senses.definitionCN: 满心想着某事，以至于注意不到其他事物
senses.example: His preoccupation with the game left him deaf to the doorbell.
senses.exampleCN: 他沉迷游戏，完全听不到门铃声。
senses.why: Something takes hold of the mind and occupies the whole space, just as a place is occupied.
senses.whyCN: 某事物抓住了心灵并占满全部空间，就像一处地方被占据了一样。

senses.title: A thing that fills your thoughts
senses.definition: the subject or worry that you think about most
senses.definitionCN: 你思考或担忧最多的话题
senses.example: Money was the chief preoccupation of the family.
senses.exampleCN: 钱是这个家庭最主要的牵挂。
senses.why: The noun also names the thing that does the occupying, not only the state.
senses.whyCN: 名词也指「占住人心的那个东西」，而不只指状态。

senses.title: Something being noticed and engaged with
senses.definition: a strong public or personal interest in an issue
senses.definitionCN: 对某议题强烈的公众或个人关注
senses.example: The emphasis on health shows the public preoccupation with diet.
senses.exampleCN: 对健康的重视体现了公众对饮食的关注。
senses.why: When many people are occupied by one topic, the word covers that shared concern.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人被同一个话题占住心思时，该词就涵盖这种共同关切。

intro.en: Preoccupation joins Latin pre- before with occupere, to seize; the medieval Latin noun preoccupatio gave the English word.
intro.cn: preoccupation 由拉丁语前缀 pre-（预先）加 occupere（占领、占据）构成，中世纪拉丁语名词 preoccupatio 是英语的来源。

items.en: Occupare means to seize or take possession of.
items.cn: occupare 意为夺取、占有。

items.en: Pre- adds the idea of doing so beforehand.
items.cn: pre- 加上「事先」之意。

items.en: Preoccupatio means a prior seizure or mental absorption.
items.cn: preoccupatio 意为预先占有或心神被占。

items.en: The word passes into French with a mental sense.
items.cn: 该词带着心理层面的含义进入法语。

items.en: English borrows it for being absorbed in a subject.
items.cn: 英语借入后表示全神贯注于某事物。

items.en: The word names both the state and the matter of concern.
items.cn: 现代英语中既指状态，也指关切之事。

note.en: Preoccupation is a cousin of occupation, preoccupied, and preoccupy, and it sits close to obsession and distraction.
note.cn: preoccupation 与 occupation、preoccupied、preoccupy 同族，与 obsession、distraction 义近。

entries.definition: a job, or the act of occupying a place
thinking about something so much as to be unaware
to fill someone thoughts completely
a thought that dominates the mind
complete engagement of the mind
something that takes the mind away

normalIntro.en: Preoccupation is pre-plus-occupation: the mind is occupied before anything else.
normalIntro.cn: preoccupation 就是 pre 加 occupation：心灵被提前占住，别的事都排不进来。

normal.en: Preoccupation and occupation share the Latin verb occupare.
normal.cn: preoccupation 与 occupation 共享拉丁语动词 occupare。

normal.en: The adjective preoccupied means lost in thought.
normal.cn: 形容词 preoccupied 表示陷入沉思。

normal.en: A preoccupation with money means money is always on your mind.
normal.cn: a preoccupation with money 指心里老是想着钱。

normal.en: The word can name the state and also the thing you care about.
normal.cn: 这个词既能指状态，也能指你关心的事。

normal.en: Compare obsession: obsession is stronger and less controlled, a preoccupation is the steady center of thought.
normal.cn: 对比 obsession：obsession 更强烈、更不受控，preoccupation 则是持续的思维中心。

abstract.en: Imagine brackets closing around one thought and leaving others outside.
abstract.cn: 想象一对括号只圈住一个念头，把其他念头都挡在外。

abstract.en: Picture a soldier putting a flag on a hill before the battle begins.
abstract.cn: 想象交战之前士兵就先把旗子插上山头。

abstract.en: Feel a hand gently tapping a table without knowing it is doing so.
abstract.cn: 感受一只手不自觉地轻敲桌面，自己却毫无察觉。

examples.en: Her preoccupation with the coming exam made her miss lunch.
examples.cn: 她一心想着即将到来的考试，连午饭都忘了吃。

examples.en: The government faces a growing preoccupation with housing costs.
examples.cn: 政府面对一个日益突出的住房成本关注点。

examples.en: He answered in a voice of preoccupation, still staring at the page.
examples.cn: 他用心不在焉的语气回答，眼睛仍盯着书页。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「提前（pre）占住（occupy）心（ation）」：心事提前占住了你整整一天，那就是 preoccupation；这只是拆词联想，与词源细节无关。

root: 拉丁语 pre-（预先）+ occupare（占领、占据）→ 中世纪拉丁语 preoccupatio → 法语 → 英语 preoccupation，核心义「预先占住、心神被占」。

sensesIntro.en: Preoccupation begins with an advance seizure, then the occupied mind, then the thing that occupies it, and finally a shared public concern.
sensesIntro.cn: preoccupation 从「预先占据」出发，接着是「被占住的心神」，然后是「占住心神的事物」，最后是共同的公众关切。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person staring at one object with the rest of the room shut out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人只盯着一样东西，把整间屋子关在外面。

branches.en: The original sense is a seizure made in advance.
branches.cn: 本义是事先做出的占领。

branches.en: The mind taken over by one idea is the mental sense.
branches.cn: 思想被一个念头占满是心理义。

branches.en: The worry itself is the thing that occupies.
branches.cn: 那份牵挂本身就是占住人心的东西。

branches.en: A public concern is the collective version.
branches.cn: 公众关切是集体层面的版本。

branches.en: Being absorbed and having a constant worry often go together.
branches.cn: 全神贯注与挥之不去的牵挂常常同时出现。

intro.en: Preoccupation is built from pre- before, the root occup, to seize, and the noun suffix -ation.
intro.cn: preoccupation 由前缀 pre-（预先）、词根 occup（占据）与名词后缀 -ation 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin occupare means to seize or fill a place; with pre- it means to seize beforehand or to fill the mind first.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 occupare 意为占领或填满一处；加上 pre- 就表示事先占据，或先占满心灵。

items.example: The prefix pre- appears in predict and prepare.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pre- 出现在 predict 与 prepare 中。

items.example: The root occup- appears in occupy.
items.exampleCN: 词根 occup- 出现在 occupy 中。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms nouns from verbs.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 由动词构成名词。

items.example: Preoccupation keeps the mental sense.
items.exampleCN: preoccupation 保留心理层面的含义。

items.example: Preoccupy drops the noun suffix.
items.exampleCN: preoccupy 去掉名词后缀。

items.meaning: to fill or take a place
items.example: Occupy is the plain English verb.
items.exampleCN: occupy 是朴素的英语动词。

items.example: The suffix -ied forms preoccupied.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ied 构成 preoccupied。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms preoccupying.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 preoccupying。

items.meaning: a job or a holding of a place
items.example: Occupation shares the same root.
items.exampleCN: occupation 共享同一词根。

definition_zh: 规定主义；订立语言规范的立场；规定式语言教学
definition_en: the belief that language should follow fixed rules and that one way of using it can be judged correct while others are wrong
core_image: 一位严格的老师在语法书上用红笔划出「该这样说」，并在窗下标上禁止通行的路牌
scene: 语言课上，老师坚持把口语里的双重否定判为错误。Many teachers once held prescriptivism and marked the local dialect wrong.
sceneCN: 这里 prescriptivism 是「规定主义」（第 1 个义项：语言有固定规则、对错可分）；句意：许多老师曾经持规定主义立场，把方言口音判为错误。

pos.zh: 规定主义；语言规范立场

collocations.zh: 道德规定主义（伦理学中的用法）

derivatives.zh: 基础词加形容词后缀构成，义为「规定的；规范性的」
基础词替换 -ism 为 -ist，义为「主张规定主义的人」
核心动词，义为「规定；开处方」
prescribe 加名词后缀，义为「规定；处方」

senses.title: The belief that language follows fixed rules
senses.definition: the view that a language has fixed rules and that some usages are correct while others are wrong
senses.definitionCN: 认为语言有固定规则、某些用法正确而另一些错误的观点
senses.example: Prescriptivism treats a split infinitive as an error.
senses.exampleCN: 规定主义把分裂不定式当成错误。
senses.why: The base prescriptive means laying down rules in advance, so the -ism names a faith in those rules.
senses.whyCN: 基础词 prescriptive 意为预先订立规则，加上 -ism 表示「信念」，于是这个词就成了一种对规则的信念。

senses.title: A teaching method based on rules
senses.definition: an approach to teaching language by giving learners explicit rules to obey
senses.definitionCN: 通过给学习者明确规则并要求遵守来进行语言教学的方法
senses.example: Their course mixed grammar drills with prescriptivism.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的课程把语法练习与规定式教学混在一起。
senses.why: If usage can be graded, the classroom will hand out the grades, so the doctrine turns into a method.
senses.whyCN: 如果用法能分对错，课堂自然就会打分，于是这种学说就转化成教学法。

senses.title: Laying down rules in ethics
senses.definition: the ethical view that moral statements tell people what they should do
senses.definitionCN: 认为道德陈述是在告诉人们应当做什么的伦理观点
senses.example: Moral prescriptivism says ought judgments guide action.
senses.exampleCN: 道德规定主义认为「应当」的判断会指导行动。
senses.why: The same word for laying down rules travels from grammar to morals.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示「订立规则」的词从语法领域挪到了道德领域，这是抽象延伸。

intro.en: Prescriptivism joins prescriptive, from Latin praescribere, to write in front or lay down, with the noun suffix -ism.
intro.cn: prescriptivism 由 prescriptive（源自拉丁语 praescribere，意为「写在前面、规定」）加名词后缀 -ism 构成。

items.en: Praescribere means to write in front, to put before, or to order.
items.cn: praescribere 意为写在前面、置于前、规定。

items.en: The noun praescriptio uses the medical sense of a written direction.
items.cn: 名词 praescriptio 继承医学中「书面指示」的含义。

items.en: Prescribe enters English from the Latin verb and keeps the sense of laying down.
items.cn: prescribe 从拉丁语动词进入英语，保留了「规定」的含义。

items.en: Prescriptive gains the sense of laying down rules for language.
items.cn: prescriptive 获得为语言订立规则的含义。

items.en: Prescriptivism is coined as the name of that doctrine and of its classroom practice.
items.cn: prescriptivism 被造出，用来命名这一学说及其课堂实践。

items.en: Linguistics contrasts prescriptivism with descriptivism.
items.cn: 现代语言学把规定主义与描述主义对照使用。

note.en: Prescriptivism names a doctrine, close in form to prescribe and prescriptive, and near in meaning to usage rules and authority.
note.cn: prescriptivism 是为一种学说命名的名词，形式上与 prescribe、prescriptive 相邻，意义上与语言规范、权威等词相邻。

entries.definition: to say what should be done or to order a medicine
laying down rules about what is correct
a person who supports this rule-based view
the view that language should be described as it is used
entries.definitionCN: 描述主义：主张如实描述语言的实际用法

entries.definition: the accepted form of a language used as a model
the way a word or language is actually used

normalIntro.en: Prescriptivism is the -ism of prescription: the habit of writing a rule in front of the language before people speak.
normalIntro.cn: prescriptivism 是「处方」的 -ism：人们开口之前，先给语言写下一张规则处方。

normal.en: Prescriptive means laying down rules, so the -ism names the doctrine.
normal.cn: prescriptive 意为订立规则，加 -ism 就是为这种主张命名。

normal.en: Its opposite is descriptivism, which describes use instead of judging it.
normal.cn: 它的反义是 descriptivism，即描述用法而不评判用法。

normal.en: The related verb prescribe also means to write out a doctor prescription.
normal.cn: 同根动词 prescribe 也指医生开处方。

normal.en: A prescriptivist is a person who holds this view.
normal.cn: prescriptivist 就是持这种观点的人。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with proscribe, which means to forbid.
normal.cn: 别和 proscribe 混淆，后者意为禁止。

abstract.en: Picture a red pen correcting grammar in the margin of a schoolbook.
abstract.cn: 想象一支红笔在课本边角改语法错误。

abstract.en: Imagine a teacher standing in front of a classroom handing out rule cards.
abstract.cn: 想象一位老师站在教室前面给每个人发规则卡。

abstract.en: Think of a signpost that tells drivers which road is lawful before they move.
abstract.cn: 想象一块路牌在车开动之前就告诉司机哪条路合规。

examples.en: Prescriptivism was strong in schools a century ago.
examples.cn: 一个世纪前，规定主义在学校里很强势。

examples.en: Modern linguists often question prescriptivism.
examples.cn: 现代语言学家常质疑规定主义。

examples.en: The article contrasts prescriptivism with a pure description of speech.
examples.cn: 这篇文章把规定主义与对口语的纯描述做了对照。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「规矩死定」——把规矩死死钉住，谁不照做就算错；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ scribere（写）→ praescribere（写在前面、规定）→ 英语 prescribe（规定）→ prescriptive（规定性的）→ prescriptivism（规定主义），核心义「先写下的规矩」。

sensesIntro.en: Prescriptivism starts as a doctrine about correct language, then becomes a teaching method, and finally lends its name to an ethical view.
sensesIntro.cn: prescriptivism 先是一个关于语言对错的学说，再变成一种教学法，最后又被借去命名一种伦理观点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red pen setting down the rules before anyone speaks.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支红笔在别人开口之前先写下规矩。

branches.en: The doctrine of correct language is the primary sense.
branches.cn: 语言对错的学说，是这个词的主要义项。

branches.en: Turning the doctrine into classroom rules gives the teaching sense.
branches.cn: 把学说变成课堂规则，就得到教学法这个义项。

branches.en: Borrowing the word for moral rules gives the ethical sense.
branches.cn: 把「订立规则」借到道德领域，就得到伦理学义项。

branches.en: Both the belief and the method rank usages from right to wrong.
branches.cn: 学说与教学法都把用法从对到错排成等级。

branches.en: Both classroom and moral versions give people rules to obey.
branches.cn: 课堂版本与道德版本都在给人可以遵守的规则。

intro.en: Prescriptivism is built on the Latin stem script, to write, with the pre- prefix and the -ive and -ism suffixes.
intro.cn: prescriptivism 建立在拉丁词干 script（写）之上，加上前缀 pre- 与后缀 -ive、-ism。

latinIntro.en: Latin scribere means to write, and praescribere adds the idea of writing in front, that is, of setting a rule down first.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scribere 意为写，praescribere 加上「写在前面」的意味，也就是先把规则写下来。

items.example: Scribere supplies the -script- core.
items.exampleCN: scribere 提供 -script- 这个核心词干。

items.example: The prefix prae- becomes pre- in English.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 prae- 在英语中变成 pre-。

items.meaning: to write in front, to lay down
items.example: Praescribere is the source of prescribe.
items.exampleCN: praescribere 是 prescribe 的来源。

items.meaning: to lay down as a rule
items.example: Prescribe keeps the laying down sense.
items.exampleCN: prescribe 保留了「规定」之义。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms prescriptive.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成 prescriptive。

items.example: Prescriptive describes language rules.
items.exampleCN: prescriptive 用来描述语言规则。

items.example: The suffix -ism turns the adjective into a doctrine.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 把形容词变成一种学说名称。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms prescriptivist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成 prescriptivist。

items.example: Proscribe looks similar but means to forbid.
items.exampleCN: proscribe 形似但意为禁止。

latinEntries.meaning: to write in front, to order
a written direction, a prefixed title

definition_zh: 预先假定；以……为前提；意味着；必然包含
definition_en: to assume something as true in advance, or to depend on something being true
core_image: 舞台开场前，道具已经摆好，观众还没意识到这些前提正撑起整场戏
scene: 讨论城市交通时，大家先默认人人都开车。The plan presupposes that every resident owns a car.
sceneCN: 这里 presuppose 是「预先假定」（第 1 个义项：把某事物预先当作真的）；句意：这个方案预先假定每位居民都拥有汽车。

pos.zh: 预先假定；以……为前提；意味着

collocations.zh: 正如该理论所预设的那样

derivatives.zh: presuppose 加名词后缀 -ition，义为「预设；前提」
基础动词，义为「假设；认为」，加前缀 pre- 得到目标词
suppose 加 -ition，义为「假定；推测」
过去分词作形容词，义为「预设的；假定的」

senses.title: To take something as true in advance
senses.definition: to assume in advance that something is true, without stating or proving it
senses.definitionCN: 在未说明或未证明的情况下预先认定某事为真
senses.example: The writer presupposes that readers share his values.
senses.exampleCN: 作者预先假定读者与他价值观相同。
senses.why: The prefix pre- adds before to suppose, so the word means to suppose first and argue later.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 pre- 给 suppose 加上「事先」的意味，也就是先假定、后论证。

senses.title: To require as a condition
senses.definition: to need something to be true or present as a condition for something else
senses.definitionCN: 以某事物的成立或存在作为另一事物的条件
senses.example: Any solution presupposes a reliable survey.
senses.exampleCN: 任何解决方案都以可靠的调查为前提。
senses.why: If the first thing is taken for granted, it turns into a bridge that the second thing must cross.
senses.whyCN: 把某事物当作理所当然，它就变成后面事物必须经过的桥，于是成为前提条件。

senses.title: To involve or imply inevitably
senses.definition: to involve something that follows inevitably from a statement or action
senses.definitionCN: 指某陈述或行为不可避免地带有的内容
senses.example: Claiming to be an expert presupposes real study.
senses.exampleCN: 自称专家必然包含着真才实学。
senses.why: Once a premise is fixed, its consequences travel with it, so the word also names what comes bundled.
senses.whyCN: 前提一旦确定，它的后果就随之而来，所以这个词也指「随之附带的含义」。

intro.en: Presuppose is Latin prae-, before, added to supponere, to put under, which gives the English verb suppose.
intro.cn: presuppose 是拉丁语前缀 prae-（在前）加到 supponere（置于下方）之上，后者演变为英语的 suppose。

items.en: Ponere means to place or put.
items.cn: ponere 意为放置、安放。

items.en: Sub- under plus ponere gives supponere, to put under.
items.cn: sub-（在下）加 ponere 构成 supponere，意为置于下方。

items.en: A form related to supponere is thought to reach Old French as supposer, to assume.
items.cn: 一般认为与 supponere 有关的形式以 supposer 进入古法语，意为假定。

items.en: Suppose enters English with the sense of assuming something to be true.
items.cn: suppose 以「假定某事为真」的含义进入英语。

items.en: Pre- is joined to suppose to make presuppose.
items.cn: 前缀 pre- 与 suppose 结合，形成 presuppose。

items.en: Logic and linguistics give it the sense of a formal premise or presupposition.
items.cn: 现代逻辑学与语言学让它带上「形式前提、预设」的含义。

note.en: Presuppose is the pre- member of the suppose family, close in form to suppose and presume, and near in meaning to assume.
note.cn: presuppose 是 suppose 词族中带 pre- 的成员，形式上与 suppose、presume 邻近，意义上与 assume 相近。

entries.definition: to think that something is probably true
something taken as true beforehand
to suppose something is true without proof
entries.definitionCN: 推测；假定（形近，但词根为 sumere，取；与 presuppose 词源不同）

entries.definition: to accept something as true without proof
to suggest something without saying it directly
to involve something as a necessary result

normalIntro.en: Presuppose is to suppose in advance: the premise is already on the table before the argument begins.
normalIntro.cn: presuppose 就是提前 suppose：论证还没开始，前提已经摆在桌上了。

normal.en: Pre- plus suppose means to suppose beforehand.
normal.cn: 前缀 pre- 加 suppose，就是「事先猜想」。

normal.en: The noun presupposition means the premise taken for granted.
normal.cn: 名词 presupposition 指被当作理所当然的前提。

normal.en: Legal writing often says a claim presupposes a duty.
normal.cn: 法律文书中常说，某项主张以某项义务为前提。

normal.en: Compare assume, which skips the pre- but keeps the same idea of taking something for granted.
normal.cn: 对比 assume：它没有前缀 pre-，但同样表示把某事视为当然。

normal.en: A presupposition is often hidden, while a stated premise is spoken aloud.
normal.cn: 预设往往藏在言外，而明说的前提则摆在台面上。

abstract.en: Picture stage props already in place before the audience arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象观众入场之前，舞台道具已经摆好。

abstract.en: Imagine a bridge built under the road, never seen but always carrying the traffic.
abstract.cn: 想象路面之下有一座桥，看不见却一直承载着车流。

abstract.en: Think of a parcel whose label says expert, with study packed silently inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一个贴着专家标签的包裹，里面默默装着真才实学。

examples.en: The question presupposes that people want to move.
examples.cn: 这个问题预先假定人们想要搬走。

examples.en: Good research presupposes honest data.
examples.cn: 好的研究以诚实的数据为前提。

examples.en: Her argument presupposes a shared definition of fairness.
examples.cn: 她的论证预设了一个共享的公平定义。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pri 先 suppose」——先用猜的，再谈证据，就是预先假定；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ sub-（在下）+ ponere（放置）→ supponere（置于下方）→ 古法语 supposer（假定）→ 英语 suppose，再加 pre- 构成 presuppose，核心义「先把假设垫在下面」。

sensesIntro.en: Presuppose begins as an advance assumption, extends to a required condition, and ends as an inevitable implication.
sensesIntro.cn: presuppose 先指事前的假定，再延伸为必需的前提条件，最后指不可避免的蕴含。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: props placed on the stage before the play begins.
core.cn: 核心意象：戏开演之前，道具已经摆上舞台。

branches.en: The advance assumption is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 事前的假定是最基本的义项。

branches.en: What is assumed becomes a condition for something else.
branches.cn: 被假定的事物转化为另一事物的条件，就是前提义项。

branches.en: What travels with a fixed premise is an implication.
branches.cn: 与既定前提一起出现的内容，成为必然蕴含的义项。

branches.en: An assumption made in advance often works as the foundation of a plan.
branches.cn: 事前的假定往往成为方案的地基。

branches.en: Both the assumption and the implication are left unstated.
branches.cn: 假定与蕴含都常常没有说出口。

intro.en: Presuppose is a Latin-built verb, combining the prefix pre-, the root pos, to place, and the English infinitive ending.
intro.cn: presuppose 是拉丁语构词法造出的动词，由前缀 pre-、词根 pos（放置）与英语动词词尾组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere means to place, and with prae- and sub- it forms supponere, to put under, and praesupponere, to put in front.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ponere 意为放置，与 prae-、sub- 组合成 supponere（置于下方）与 praesupponere（置于在前）。

items.example: The prefix prae- becomes pre- in English.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 prae- 在英语中写作 pre-。

items.example: Sub- combines with ponere to form supponere.
items.exampleCN: sub- 与 ponere 结合成 supponere。

items.example: Ponere gives the -pos- root seen in suppose.
items.exampleCN: ponere 提供 suppose 中的 -pos- 词根。

items.example: Supponere is the ancestor of suppose.
items.exampleCN: supponere 是 suppose 的祖先。

items.example: Suppose is the base for the longer verb.
items.exampleCN: suppose 是更长动词的基础。

items.meaning: to place, as in compose and dispose
items.meaningCN: 放置（见于 compose、dispose 等词）
items.example: The form -pose shows the family likeness.
items.exampleCN: 词形 -pose 显示词族相似。

items.meaning: to take something as true beforehand
items.example: Presuppose adds pre- to suppose.
items.exampleCN: presuppose 在 suppose 前加上 pre-。

items.meaning: a noun-forming ending for an action
items.example: The suffix -ition forms presupposition.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ition 构成 presupposition。

items.example: Presupposition names the assumed premise.
items.exampleCN: presupposition 指被假定的前提。

definition_zh: 自命不凡；做作；声称；主张
definition_en: the act of claiming something you do not really have, or a showy claim to importance or quality
core_image: 一件外套被撑得鼓鼓的，里面其实空无一物
scene: 那家新开的餐厅装潢华美，菜却平平。The place has no pretension to fine dining, yet its prices are high.
sceneCN: 这里 pretension 是「声称；自命」（第 1 个义项：自称拥有某种身份或品质）；句意：这家店并不自称高档餐饮，但价格却很高。

pos.zh: 自命不凡；做作；声称；主张

derivatives.zh: pretension 加 -ious 构成，义为「自命不凡的；做作的」
核心动词，义为「假装；自称」，pretension 由其同源名词而来
pretend 的同源名词，义为「假装；托词」（英式拼写）
pretentious 加否定前缀 un-，义为「不摆架子的；谦逊的」

senses.title: A claim to have something one lacks
senses.definition: a claim to possess a quality, rank, or right that may not really belong to someone
senses.definitionCN: 声称拥有某种品质、地位或权利，而实际上未必拥有
senses.example: The town has pretensions to being a cultural capital.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小城自命为文化之都。
senses.why: The root ten means to stretch out, so the word pictures a claim stretched forward for all to see.
senses.whyCN: 词根 ten 意为伸展，这个词因此描绘一只手向前伸出、向众人展示的声称。

senses.title: Showy behaviour to impress others
senses.definition: a showy, affected way of behaving or speaking meant to impress others
senses.definitionCN: 为了给人留下印象而故作姿态、矫揉造作的言行
senses.example: His lecture was full of style and pretension.
senses.exampleCN: 他的讲座满是花哨的风格与做作。
senses.why: When the outward claim outweighs the inward substance, the claim becomes a show, which is pretension.
senses.whyCN: 当外在的声称超过内在的实质，声称就成了一场表演，这就是做作。

senses.title: An ambition or aspiration
senses.definition: a serious ambition to rise to a certain standard or position
senses.definitionCN: 想达到某种水准或地位的严肃抱负
senses.example: The small school has real pretensions to academic excellence.
senses.exampleCN: 这所小学校确实有追求学术卓越的抱负。
senses.why: The same forward reach can be read as mere vanity or as a genuine reach for something higher.
senses.whyCN: 同一种向外伸展，既可读作虚荣，也可读作真诚地追求更高目标。

intro.en: Pretension comes through French from Latin praetendere, to stretch in front, which joins prae-, before, with tendere, to stretch.
intro.cn: pretension 经法语来自拉丁语 praetendere（向前伸展），由 prae-（在前）与 tendere（伸展）构成。

items.en: Tendere means to stretch or spread out.
items.cn: tendere 意为伸展或铺开。

items.en: Prae- before plus tendere gives praetendere, to stretch out in front.
items.cn: prae-（在前）加 tendere 构成 praetendere，意为向前伸展。

items.en: Pretext and pretence carry the stretching image into French usage.
items.cn: pretext 与 pretence 把「向前伸展」的意象带入法语用法。

items.en: Pretension enters English with the sense of claiming or alleging.
items.cn: pretension 以「声称、主张」的含义进入英语。

items.en: The word develops the modern sense of showy, empty claims to importance.
items.cn: 在十八至十九世纪，这个词发展出「华而不实、自命不凡」的现代含义。

items.en: Pretentious, formed from a related stem, becomes the common adjective.
items.cn: 由相关词干构成的 pretentious 成为常用形容词。

note.en: Pretension is the noun of claiming, close in form to pretentious and pretence, and near in meaning to arrogance and affectation.
note.cn: pretension 是一个表示「声称、自命」的名词，形式上与 pretentious、pretence 相邻，意义上与傲慢、做作相近。

entries.definition: to act as if something were true when it is not
showing off importance that is not deserved
the act of pretending or a false excuse
unpleasant pride and a belief that one is superior
artificial behaviour put on to impress
a strong desire to achieve something

normalIntro.en: Pretension is a claim stretched out in front: the hand reaches forward to show what may not be there.
normalIntro.cn: pretension 是向前伸出的声称：手向前一伸，展示的却未必真实存在。

normal.en: Pretend means to put something in front, and pretension is the noun of that reach.
normal.cn: pretend 意为把某事物摆到前面，pretension 就是这一伸展动作的名词。

normal.en: The adjective pretentious describes a person full of pretension.
normal.cn: 形容词 pretentious 描述充满 pretension 的人。

normal.en: Without pretension means modest and natural.
normal.cn: without pretension 意为朴实自然、不摆架子。

normal.en: Pre- means in front, and the root ten means to stretch.
normal.cn: 前缀 pre- 表示在前，词根 ten 表示伸展。

normal.en: Do not forget the base verb pretend, which keeps the same claim image.
normal.cn: 别忘了基础动词 pretend，它保留了同样的「声称」意象。

abstract.en: Picture a coat puffed up on a hanger with nothing inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一件外套在衣架上撑得鼓鼓的，里面却空无一物。

abstract.en: Imagine someone speaking in a voice too grand for the room.
abstract.cn: 想象有人用比房间本身宏大得多的腔调说话。

abstract.en: Think of a hand stretched forward holding nothing but open air.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手向前伸出，握着的只有空气。

examples.en: She had no pretensions to greatness.
examples.cn: 她并不自命不凡。

examples.en: The old hotel is comfortable and free of pretension.
examples.cn: 这家老酒店舒适而不做作。

examples.en: His pretensions to expertise annoyed the panel.
examples.cn: 他自命专业的姿态让评审团反感。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拼天分」——表面拼命展示天分，其实只是自吹；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ tendere（伸展）→ praetendere（向前伸展）→ 法语 pretension → 英语 pretension，核心义「把没有的东西伸出去给人看」。

sensesIntro.en: Pretension begins as a forward claim, turns into a showy manner, and can end up as mere aspiration.
sensesIntro.cn: pretension 先指向前的声称，再转化为故作姿态，最后也可仅指志在更高。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coat puffed up with nothing inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件撑得鼓鼓、内里空无一物的外套。

branches.en: The forward claim is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 向前的声称是最基本的义项。

branches.en: A claim with more show than substance becomes affectation.
branches.cn: 声称超过实质，就变成做作。

branches.en: The same reach, read kindly, is an ambition.
branches.cn: 同一种伸展若作善意理解，就是抱负。

branches.en: A claim and an ambition both look upward toward a higher rank.
branches.cn: 声称与抱负都向上看，指向更高的位置。

branches.en: Showy words and sincere hope can wear the same outward style.
branches.cn: 做作的言辞与真诚的期望在表面上可能一样。

intro.en: Pretension is built on the Latin root tend, to stretch, with the pre- prefix and the -ion noun ending, and it pairs with pretend and pretentious.
intro.cn: pretension 建立在拉丁词根 tend（伸展）之上，配以前缀 pre- 与名词后缀 -ion，并与 pretend、pretentious 同族。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere means to stretch, and praetendere adds prae-, in front, so the verb means to stretch something forward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tendere 意为伸展，praetendere 加上 prae-（在前），动词意为把某物向前伸展。

items.example: Tendere supplies the -ten- root.
items.exampleCN: tendere 提供 -ten- 词根。

items.example: The prefix prae- becomes pre- in English.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 prae- 在英语中写作 pre-。

items.meaning: to stretch out in front, to claim
items.example: Praetendere is the ultimate source of pretend.
items.exampleCN: praetendere 是 pretend 的最终来源。

items.example: Pretend keeps the claim image.
items.exampleCN: pretend 保留了「声称」的意象。

items.example: Pretentious describes a showy person.
items.exampleCN: pretentious 描述爱显摆的人。

items.meaning: a noun-forming ending for an action
items.example: The suffix -ion turns the verb into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 把动词变成名词。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unpretentious.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unpretentious。

items.example: Unpretentious means modest in manner.
items.exampleCN: unpretentious 意为不摆架子。

items.meaningCN: 紧绷的（同源于 tendere 的英语词）
items.example: Tense shares the stretching root.
items.exampleCN: tense 共享「伸展」词根。

definition_zh: 自命不凡的；炫耀的；做作的；矫饰的
definition_en: trying to appear more important, clever, or cultured than you really are
core_image: 衣领挺得过高的演员，在舞台上摆出并不属于他的派头
scene: 面试的年轻人满口大词，考官却觉得他只是在摆样子。The young man in the interview kept using big words, and the examiner felt he was being pretentious.
sceneCN: 这里 pretentious 是「自命不凡、炫耀做作」（第 1 个义项：想显得比自己实际更重要或更有学问）；句意：面试的年轻人满口大词，考官却觉得他只是在摆样子。

pos.zh: 自命不凡的；炫耀的；做作的

collocations.zh: 给人留下装腔作势的印象

derivatives.zh: -ness 名词化：自命不凡，做作的派头
同根名词：自称、要求，常指做作的派头或名不副实的主张
-ly 副词化：装腔作势地，故作高深地
同根动词：假装，语感比形容词轻，但不一定带贬义

senses.title: Inflated self-importance
senses.definition: acting, looking, or speaking as if you were more important than you are
senses.definitionCN: 举止、外表或谈吐显得比实际更重要
senses.example: The restaurant is expensive and faintly pretentious.
senses.exampleCN: 那家餐厅很贵，还略带自命不凡的派头。
senses.why: The Latin verb praetendere meant to stretch something out in front, so a person who pretends is literally holding up a front.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praetendere 本义是「伸到前面」，所以假装的人其实是在身前举一块招牌，自命不凡正是这块招牌。

senses.title: Showy culture or learning
senses.definition: showing off knowledge or good taste in a way that feels forced
senses.definitionCN: 以一种生硬的方式卖弄学问或品味
senses.example: Her essay is full of pretentious quotations.
senses.exampleCN: 她的文章塞满了故作高深的引语。
senses.why: Any claim held in front of others can be knowledge as well as rank, so the same word labels showy quotations and trendy decoration.
senses.whyCN: 举在别人面前的主张既可以是地位，也可以是学问，所以同一个词也用来形容卖弄的引语和时髦的装饰。

senses.title: Pompous in style
senses.definition: using grand or elaborate style where plain words would do
senses.definitionCN: 本该用平实说法的场合却使用夸张繁复的风格
senses.example: The film is beautiful but rather pretentious.
senses.exampleCN: 那部电影很美，却相当故作高深。
senses.why: When the display of importance passes from a person into a film, a novel, or a speech, it becomes a style that reaches for grandeur it has not earned.
senses.whyCN: 当「摆派头」从人转到电影、小说或演讲上时，它就成了一种追求配不上的宏大的风格。

intro.en: Pretentious comes from Latin prae- before and tendere to stretch, through the noun praetensio, a stretching out.
intro.cn: pretentious 来自拉丁语 prae-（在前）加 tendere（伸展），经名词 praetensio（向前伸、张力）而来。

items.en: Prae- meant before or in front, the same prefix that gives prepare and predict.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在前、在……前面」，prepare 与 predict 也用的是这个前缀。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch, and it supplies the tent- seen in tension and attention.
items.cn: tendere 意为「伸展」，tension 与 attention 里的 tent- 都源自它。

items.en: Praetendere meant to stretch something out in front or raise it as a cover, and it is the ancestor of pretend.
items.cn: praetendere 意为「向前伸出」，或举起某物作遮挡，它是 pretend 的祖先。

items.en: The noun praetensio named a stretching out and also a showy claim or assertion.
items.cn: 名词 praetensio 既指「向前伸展」，也指夸耀的主张或断言。

items.en: The Latin adjective praetentiosus passed into French as pretentieux, carrying the sense of a claim put on display.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词 praetentiosus 进入法语作 pretentieux，带着「把主张摆出来给人看」的意思。

items.en: English took the adjective in the nineteenth century, and its modern sense settled on claiming a rank or learning that is not really there.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪吸收了这个形容词，现代义固化为「冒充并不真正拥有的地位或学问」。

note.en: Pretentious is a claim put on show, so it sits near pretend and pretension by form, and near pompous, ostentatious, and affected by meaning.
note.cn: pretentious 是「摆出来给人看的架子」，所以形式上靠近 pretend 与 pretension，意义上靠近 pompous、ostentatious 与 affected。

entries.definition: to act as if something is true when it is not
entries.definitionCN: 假装；同根：拉丁语「伸到前面」

entries.definition: a claim to importance or culture that may not be deserved
entries.definitionCN: 自称，常指做作的派头或名不副实的声称

entries.definition: a false appearance or claim, spelled pretence in British English
entries.definitionCN: 假装；借口，英式拼作 pretence

entries.definition: too serious and full of self-importance in manner or speech
entries.definitionCN: 自大的；浮夸的，强调自我感觉良好

entries.definition: designed to attract notice and show wealth or importance
entries.definitionCN: 炫耀的；卖弄的，强调故意让人看见

entries.definition: behaving in an artificial way, put on to impress others
entries.definitionCN: 做作的；不自然的，强调行为不真

normalIntro.en: Pretentious belongs with pretend: both stretch something out in front of others to be admired.
normalIntro.cn: pretentious 与 pretend 同宗：都是把某样东西伸到别人眼前求人称赞。

normal.en: The -ous ending makes it an adjective, so pretentious describes people, films, and speech.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ous 把它变成形容词，所以 pretentious 形容人、影片和语言。

normal.en: Pretension is the noun of the same family and names the claim itself.
normal.cn: pretension 是同族名词，指的就是那份「主张」本身。

normal.en: Compare pretend: to pretend is to act it out, to be pretentious is to carry that act around.
normal.cn: 对比 pretend：pretend 是演出来，pretentious 则是把那场戏随身带着。

normal.en: A pretentious display of knowledge means showing off learning nobody asked for.
normal.cn: a pretentious display of knowledge 指没人要求时还硬要卖弄学问。

normal.en: Pretentious is usually a judgement from the outside, so a writer can be called pretentious by a plain reader.
normal.cn: pretentious 通常是外人的评价，所以普通读者也可以说一位作者故作高深。

abstract.en: Picture someone lifting a grand sign above their head so the room cannot miss it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把一块气派的牌子举过头顶，让全场都无法忽视。

abstract.en: Picture a lecture full of long Latin words that nobody in the room needs.
abstract.cn: 想象一场演讲塞满拉丁长词，而满屋人根本用不上。

abstract.en: Picture an art film where every slow scene is meant to look deeper than it is.
abstract.cn: 想象一部文艺片，每个慢镜头都刻意显得比实际更深。

examples.en: He wears a pretentious watch to remind everyone of his success.
examples.cn: 他戴着炫耀性的名表，好让每个人都想起他的成功。

examples.en: The menu is written in pretentious French with a tiny footnote in English.
examples.cn: 菜单用故作讲究的法语写成，只在脚注里附了一行小字英文。

examples.en: Critics called the novel pretentious rather than profound.
examples.cn: 评论家认为这部小说不是深刻，而是故作高深。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来身子」——往前一扑、硬要占前排，正是自命不凡的架势；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ tendere（伸展）→ praetendere（伸到前面；举作遮挡）＋形容词词尾 -ious → 英语 pretentious，核心义「把架子摆到别人面前」。

sensesIntro.en: Pretentious first describes a person pretending to more importance, then the showy display of learning, and finally a style that strains to look deep.
sensesIntro.cn: pretentious 先形容人自命不凡，再指卖弄学问或品味，最后形容作品风格故作高深。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grand sign held above the head so the room cannot miss it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块气派的牌子被高举过头，让全场都无法忽视。

branches.en: A person claiming undeserved importance is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 自称拥有配不上的地位，是日常义项。

branches.en: Showy learning is the same claim applied to knowledge.
branches.cn: 卖弄学问是同一份主张用在知识上。

branches.en: The strained style is the claim carried by a work rather than a person.
branches.cn: 故作高深的风格是主张由作品而非人来承载。

branches.en: A dinner guest who names every wine and every dish is both self-important and showy.
branches.cn: 在饭桌上把每一款酒、每一道菜都点评一遍的客人，既自命不凡又爱卖弄。

branches.en: Both showy quotations and an overloaded style reach for a depth that is not there.
branches.cn: 卖弄的引语与堆砌的风格，都在追求一种并不存在的深度。

intro.en: Pretentious is built from Latin prae- and tendere plus the adjective ending -ious, and the stem -tent- links it to pretend and tension.
intro.cn: pretentious 由拉丁前缀 prae-、词根 tendere 与形容词词尾 -ious 组成，词干 -tent- 又把它和 pretend、tension 连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin prae- means in front, and the verb tendere means to stretch, so praetendere is to stretch out before.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prae- 意为「在前」，动词 tendere 意为「伸展」，合起来 praetendere 就是「伸到前面」。

items.example: The prefix prae- places the act ahead of the eyes.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 prae- 把这个动作放到众人眼前。

items.exampleCN: tendere 提供 attention 与 tension 中的「伸展」。

items.example: The root tent- appears in tension and intent.
items.exampleCN: 词根 tent- 出现在 tension 和 intent 里。

items.meaning: to stretch out in front, to put forward as a cover

items.exampleCN: praetendere 是 pretend 的直接祖先。

items.example: The suffix -tiosus turns the claim into an adjective of character.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tiosus 把「主张」变成描述性格的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ious forms pretentious from the stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ious 由词干构成 pretentious。

items.meaning: a claim to importance or culture

items.exampleCN: pretension 指形容词背后那份主张。

items.meaning: to act as if something is true

items.exampleCN: pretend 保留着「举在前面」的字面意象。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms pretentiousness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 pretentiousness。
